purpose: The primary standalone recipe collection loaded by the Shopping Assistant meal planner.
content_note: The primary standalone collection, now including the Food Fusion catalog. Recipe facts and ingredient quantities are normalized; Food Fusion directions are independently formulated. Food Fusion images and source-page links are excluded.

variant_model.approach: Regional or materially distinct protein, sauce or technique variants remain separate under one dish family. Near-identical versions are merged. International dishes are included only when they represent recognizably different recipes commonly cooked in Pakistani homes.

Fatima Cooks.mode: previously extracted local dataset; no new crawl

curated_home_style_additions.approach: Independently developed and standardized for the meal planner; no external recipe prose copied.

nutrition_methodology.source_values: Retained when supplied by the recipe card.
nutrition_methodology.missing_values: Estimated from normalized ingredient quantities and a compact food-composition table, then divided by the stated yield. Every recipe labels its basis, confidence and ingredient weight coverage. Estimates are for meal planning, not clinical use.
nutrition_methodology.serving_and_macro_reconciliation: When a source omitted yield, servings were estimated from ingredient volume and labelled. Estimated missing macros were scaled only when needed to remain consistent with a plausible source-reported calorie value.

variants.name: Punjabi Achar Gosht

handful Hara Dhaniya aur Hari Mirch (Fresh Coriander and Green Chillies)

instructions: Warm the tel (oil) in a handi (pot) or degh (heavy pot) on high until it's smoking-hot — test by dropping in one mustard seed; Stir in all five achari spices: zeera, raie, saunf, kalonji, and methi dana.
Stir in the sliced pyaz (onions) to the spiced oil. Spread them out and cook on medium-high heat, stirring every few minutes. Aim for them deep golden-brown — the colour of a digestive biscuit.

Stir in the adrak lahsun paste (ginger-garlic paste) and stir constantly for 90 seconds on high heat until the raw smell disappears and it turns a slightly darker colour. Stir in lal mirch powder and dhaniya powder. Stir for another 30 seconds — the dry spices will clump.

Stir in the chopped tamatar (tomatoes) and turn heat to medium-high. Stir everything together and cook uncovered for 15-20 minutes, crushing the tomatoes with your chamcha (ladle) as they soften. Cook until the tomatoes have completely disintegrated into the masala and the tel (oil) has separated and is.

Stir in the gosht (meat) pieces to the masala. Turn heat to high and bhuno (stir-Cook) the meat for 5-6 minutes, turning each piece so every surface gets coated in masala and seared. You'll hear a loud sizzling and the meat will change colour from red to a.
Reduce heat to medium-low. Stir in the dahi (yoghurt) in a slow stream, stirring constantly as you pour. Once it's incorporated, Stir in half a cup of paani (water).

Once the gosht is tender, remove the lid, turn heat to medium-high, and stir-cook the curry for another 5-8 minutes to evaporate excess liquid and concentrate the flavours. The flavour should be sharp, tangy from the achari spices and tomatoes, with heat from the mirch.
Scatter a generous handful of chopped hara dhaniya (fresh coriander) and a few slit hari mirchein (green chillies) over the top.

Saute for five minutes and Stir in a tablespoon or more of water to prevent the potatoes from sticking to the bottom of the pot.

Stir in POTATOES — TIMING IS EVERYTHING: Once gosht is tender, Stir in potato pieces. Stir in hot water if needed. Cook on medium heat 20-22 minutes until potatoes are just tender.
THE LAHORI FINISHING TOUCH — FRESH GARAM MASALA OFF HEAT: Take the pot off the heat. Stir in fresh garam masala (freshly ground is best), slit hari mirch, and most of the hara dhania. Stir gently.

instructions: Peel potatoes and cut into thick rounds (about 1.5cm) or halve small potatoes. Par-boil in salted water for 8 minutes — they should be partially cooked but still firm in the centre. Drain and let steam off for 5 minutes.
Warm oil in a karahi (wok) to 170°C. Cook potato rounds in batches for 5-6 minutes until a pale golden colour forms and they're nearly cooked through. Remove and drain.
This is the tuk technique — the pressing creates the signature shape.
Return oil to 190°C (hotter than first Cook). Cook the pressed rounds in batches for 3-4 minutes until deep golden, crispy, and sizzling vigorously. Drain on a wire rack.
While still hot, Mix all the dry spices and sprinkle generously over aloo tuk. Toss gently to coat all surfaces.
Garnish with hara dhania.

alternate_methods.label: Alternate documented method
instructions: Cut each potato into thick, even slices — about 1 to 1.5 cm thick (roughly the thickness of two stacked 10-rupee coins). Try to make all the slices as even as possible so they cook at the same rate. Rinse the slices in cold water to remove surface.
In a small bowl, mix together the namak (salt), amchoor (dry mango powder), lal mirch powder (red chilli), chaat masala, and zeera powder (cumin powder). Mix well.
Pour oil into a karahi (wok) to at least 3 inches depth. Heat the oil to medium heat — approximately 160–170°C. Carefully Stir in the potato slices in a single layer — don't overcrowd.
While the potatoes are still hot from the first Cook, Put them one by one on a flat surface (a plate or cutting board).

Increase the oil heat to high — Aim for the oil hot , approximately 180–190°C. Test with a tiny bread cube: it should brown in 30–40 seconds. Carefully Stir in the pressed potato slices back into the hot oil in batches.

Transfer the freshly fried hot potatoes directly into a large bowl or onto a serving plate. Toss gently (use a spoon or shake the plate) to coat every slice. The heat from the potatoes will toast the spices slightly against the surface, intensifying their flavour.

In a large, heavy-bottomed pot or pressure cooker, Mix the beef mince, soaked and drained chana dal, roughly chopped onion, garlic cloves, ginger, cinnamon sticks, black cardamom, green cardamom, cloves, cumin seeds, coriander seeds, button red chillies, black peppercorns, salt, red chilli powder, and turmeric powder. Stir in.
Transfer to a food processor in batches and pulse until the meat and dal are finely ground together — the texture should be smooth but not a paste.

Transfer the ground mixture to a large mixing bowl. Stir in the finely chopped onion, fresh coriander, green chillies, mint leaves, and 1 beaten egg. Mix thoroughly with your hands until everything is evenly incorporated.

Take about 1⁄4 cup of the mixture and shape it into a flat, round patty about 1⁄2-inch thick — roughly the diameter of your burger bun. Refrigerate for 20–30 minutes to firm up — this step is crucial for clean frying.

Warm a non-stick tawa or frying pan over medium heat with 2–3 tablespoons of oil. In a shallow bowl, beat 2 eggs for the egg wash. Shallow-Cook for 3–4 minutes per side until deep golden brown and crispy on the outside.

In the same tawa, Cook the eggs for the burger topping. Crack one egg per burger onto the hot tawa and cook sunny-side up or break the yolk and spread it thin (Lahori street style). Season with a pinch of salt, black pepper, and a dash of red.
Toast the cut sides on the tawa with a little oil or butter until golden. On the bottom half, spread a generous layer of green chutney. Stir in a drizzle of tamarind chutney (if using).

variants.name: Bajra Roti

ingredients.text: 2 cups bajra ka atta (pearl millet flour)
3 tablespoons ghee ya makhan (ghee or butter)

instructions: Bajra ka atta is grey-brown, smells distinctly earthy and nutty, and contains no gluten whatsoever. Like makki ka atta, this means you cannot roll it thin with a belan — it will crack apart.

Put the bajra ka atta in a wide bowl and Stir in the salt. Stir in warm water slowly, mixing with your hand as you go. Knead into a firm, smooth dough — it won't be as smooth as wheat dough, but it should hold together without crumbling.
Put your tawa (flat griddle pan) on medium heat. Allow it to heat for 2–3 minutes. Bajra roti cooks on medium heat — not as low as makki roti, but not as high as chapati.
Divide the dough into 4 portions.
Carefully Put the shaped roti on the warm tawa. Cook for 2.5–3 minutes. The bottom will become firm and develop golden-brown patches, and the top surface will look dry and set.
Cook the second side for 2.5–3 minutes until evenly golden and firm when you press the centre.
Bajra roti hardens as it cools — it becomes a dry, crumbly disk within 10–15 minutes.

instructions: In a small bowl, Mix lukewarm water, 1 teaspoon of the sugar, and yeast. Stir once and leave 8–10 minutes until foamy.
Mix flour, remaining sugar, salt, and cardamom powder in a large paraat. Stir in the yeast mixture and oil. Knead for 8 minutes until smooth.
Cover and rest in a warm spot for 45 minutes to 1 hour until the dough has puffed and is noticeably lighter.
Take one portion and roll it out on a lightly floured chakla into a thin rectangle or oval shape, as thin as you can get it without tearing — roughly 3–4mm thick.
Put the folded dough squares on a lightly floured surface. Cover with a cloth and rest for 15 minutes.

After resting, take one folded square and gently roll it out with the belan into a round or oval shape about 15–18cm across and 5–6mm thick. Roll gently and evenly — do not press too hard or you will flatten the layers you worked so hard to create.
Set your oven to 200°C (390°F) with a baking tray inside preheating. Brush the top of each shaped bakarkhani with egg yolk wash — this gives the classic deep golden-brown colour.
Slide the bakarkhani onto the hot baking tray and bake at 200°C for 12–15 minutes until deep golden brown and crisp.
Remove from the oven and let rest for 5 minutes.

variants.name: Balochi Rosh

ingredients.text: 1.5 kg bakra (goat) or mutton, bone-in pieces

instructions: Rinse the pot with water and shake out excess — a wet pot helps prevent early sticking.

Scatter the cracked badi elaichi (black cardamom), laung (cloves), kali mirch (black peppercorns), and darchini (cinnamon stick) directly over the meat. Do not grind them, do not Stir in ginger, garlic, onion, tomato, or any powder spice.
Pour the 100ml of pani (water) into the pot — just enough to cover the base. The water will cook off within 20-30 minutes.
Put the pot on your stove over medium heat to start. Aim for to hear a gentle sizzle and see steam beginning to build — not a violent boil.
After 10 minutes, turn the heat to low — as low as your stove goes while still producing heat. Set your timer for 3 hours and walk away. Do not stir.
After 3 hours, carefully lift the lid away from you (steam is very hot — it will burn). If there is any resistance, re-seal and cook for another 30-45 minutes.
Taste the broth. Do not Stir in anything else. Turn off the heat and let the Rosh rest in the pot, lid on, for 10 minutes before serving.

ingredients.text: 1 kg beef (bone-in, shanks or short ribs)

instructions: Stir in 2 litres of cold water, the black cardamom, cloves, cinnamon sticks, bay leaves, black peppercorns, ginger, and garlic. Do NOT Stir in the onions or salt yet. Bring to a boil over high heat.
As the water comes to a boil, a grey foam will appear on the surface — this is impurities from the meat.

While the beef simmers, heat the oil or Raha ghee in a separate small karahi (wok) or frying pan over medium-high heat. Stir in the sliced onions and Cook, stirring often, for 15-20 minutes until they are deep golden brown — think the colour of dark honey.

When the beef is tender, use a chimta (tongs) to remove the beef pieces and set them aside on a plate. Strain the broth through a fine sieve or colander into a bowl to remove all the whole spices. pour the strained broth back into the large degh.
Bring the seasoned broth to a rolling boil over high heat. Stir in the drained soaked basmati rice directly into the boiling broth. Stir once gently with a chamcha (ladle).
Put the reserved beef pieces gently on top of the rice. Reduce the heat to the absolute lowest setting. Cover the degh with a tight-fitting lid.
After 20 minutes, turn off the heat and let the pot rest undisturbed for 10 minutes. Arrange the beef pieces on top and serve immediately.

instructions: Before you start the halwa, prepare the chashni (sugar syrup) so it's ready to pour when needed. In a pateela (saucepan), Mix 0.75 cup cheeni and 1.5 cups paani. Heat on medium, stirring until the sugar dissolves completely.

In your heaviest karahi (wok) or a thick-bottomed degh (heavy-bottomed pot), melt the ghee on medium heat. Once the ghee is melted and hot (you'll see it shimmer), reduce to medium-low heat. Stir in the sifted besan all at once and start stirring immediately with a chamcha (ladle).

Over the next 20-25 minutes on medium-low heat, the besan will go through several visible and olfactory stages. Stage 1 (first 5 minutes): Pale yellow, raw smell of chickpea flour. Stage 2 (5-12 minutes): The mixture begins to dry out and look slightly grainy.

Stir in THE SYRUP — STAND BACK: This is the dangerous-beautiful moment. Reduce the heat to low. Pour the syrup slowly into the hot roasted besan in a steady stream while simultaneously stirring vigorously.

Increase heat back to medium and keep stirring the halwa. As you stir and cook, the mixture will absorb the moisture and tighten up. Cook for 8-12 minutes, stirring continuously, until the halwa thickens and begins to pull away cleanly from the sides and bottom of the karahi.
Transfer the halwa to a serving plate or individual shikoras (clay bowls). Garnish with sliced pista and badam arranged decoratively on top.

ingredients.text: 300 grams bhee ya kamal kakdi (lotus stem)
1 tsp lal mirch powder (red chilli powder)

instructions: Rinse thoroughly under running water, paying attention to the hollow channels inside the stem where soil can hide. As you cut through it, you'll see the beautiful lacy pattern of hollow tubes — this is what makes bhee so distinctive and lovely. If using canned bhee, simply drain.

Put the sliced bhee in a pateela (saucepan) and cover with water. Stir in 1/4 tsp salt and 1/4 tsp haldi. Bring to a boil and cook for 5–7 minutes until the bhee is just slightly softened but still has a firm bite — test by pressing a.

Warm 4 tbsp of oil in a karahi (wok) over medium heat. Stir in the whole sabut garam masala (cloves, cardamom, cinnamon). Stir in the sliced pyaz (onion) and Cook for 10–12 minutes, stirring regularly, until deep golden brown.

Stir in the blended or finely chopped tamatar (tomatoes). Stir everything together and cook for 5–6 minutes until the tomatoes have broken down completely and the masala is thick. Stir in all the ground spices: haldi, lal mirch powder, dhania powder, zeera powder, amchoor, and namak.

Stir in TAMARIND, BHEE, AND ALOO: Stir in the imli (tamarind) paste — the masala will immediately smell bright and tangy. Stir in the par-boiled bhee slices and the cubed aloo (potatoes). Stir gently to coat everything in the masala.
Cover the karahi with a lid and cook on medium-low heat for 15–18 minutes, stirring gently every 5 minutes to prevent sticking. If the masala is too dry, Stir in 2–3 tablespoons of water.

Garnish generously with fresh hara dhania (coriander). The dish should have a thick, clinging masala, beautiful lotus stem coins nestled among golden potato cubes, and a colour that is a deep, rich reddish-brown.

Proceed by add water,pink salt,mix well; cook for 1-2 minutes.
Tadka: In a tadka pan Add cooking oil,onion,garlic and fry for a minute.
Add cumin seeds,button red chillies,mix well and fry until golden.
Pour tadka in daal,mix well; serve!
Green Coconut Chutney: In bending jug,Add mint leaves,fresh corinader,garlic,green chillies,desiccated coconut,caster sugar,pink salt,lemon juice,cooking oil,water and blend until smooth.
Assembling: Combine the listed ingredients; serve! In the serving bowl.

variants.name: Bhuna Gosht Masala - Lamb Bhuna
instructions: Prepare all ingredients before heating the pan.
Warm the cooking fat and cook onion, heaped tsp garlic paste, heaped tsp ginger paste, red chilli powder until softened and aromatic.
Stir in cumin powder, coriander powder, red chilli powder, coarsely ground black pepper, garam masala, kashmiri chilli powder/degi mirch, then add the lamb and coat it thoroughly in the masala.
Add the listed liquid ingredients as needed, cover and simmer until the main ingredient is fully cooked.
Reduce the sauce to the intended consistency, adjust the seasoning and finish with heaped tsp ginger paste, coriander powder, coriander.

variants.name: Pakistani Style Bhuna Gosht (Instant Pot & Stove Top)
instructions: Put the IP on Saute mode (high heat) and heat about 1/4 cup of oil. Once the oil is hot Stir in the cumin seeds, let them sizzle.
And then Stir in the onions and cook until they've completely softened and the edges start to turn golden. Stir in the garlic and ginger paste, cook for 60 seconds.
Stir in the salt, red chili powder, turmeric powder, coriander powder and the beef cubes, mix, and brown the cubes well. Stir in the chopped tomatoes and 2 cups of water.

Put the Instant Pot on manual (high pressure) for 30 minutes. Open the Instant Pot and cook on saute (high) and dry up the Masala - this takes about 15 minutes, you don't need to do much for the first ten or so.

When the masala dries and the mixture starts to stick to the bottom and then cook for a few minutes until the mixture darkens. If it starts to stick Stir in a little oil. Stir in the yogurt, mix well, cook for two minutes.
Stir in the Garam Masala, taste and adjust seasoning.

alternate_methods.label: Alternate documented method
instructions: Mix the yogurt, crushed garlic and ginger, salt, red chili, garam masala, and cumin powder in a large bowl. Stir in the chopped beef and turn to coat. Cover and refrigerate for a minimum of 1 hour and up to 8 hours.
Warm oil in a heavy-bottomed pot over medium-low heat until it begins to shimmer. Stir in the chopped onion and Cook until they soften and brown at the edges, about 7 to 10 minutes.
Increase heat to medium-high, and Stir in the beef with the yogurt marinade. Cook until evenly brown, about 5 minutes.
Stir in the crushed tomatoes, and 1 cup of water. Cover and bring to boil.

Lower to a gentle simmer. Let the beef cook, with the lid still on, on low heat for 2 to 2 1⁄2 hours until tender. Stir and Stir in small amounts of water (no more than 1⁄4 cup at a time), occasionally, to prevent it from sticking to.

Once soft, bring heat to medium-high, and briefly stir until the oil begins to separate, about 2 to 3 minutes. Stir in 1 to 2 tablespoon of water if necessary. Remove from heat and transfer to serving bowl.

Proceed by add yogurt,mix well; cook until oil separates (2-3 minutes).

Add roasted spices and grind to make a coarse powder. In a spice mixer.
Add fried onion,blend again; reserve.
Add beef boneless cubes,salt,mustard oil and mix well. In a bowl.
Add the listed ingredients and grinded onion and spices mixture and mix well,cover and marinate for 4-6 hours.
Add cooking oil and marinated beef and mix well. In a pot.
Cover; cook over low heat until beef is tender (approx. 40-45 minutes).

Kashmiri lal mirch (Kashmiri red chilli) Powder 1 tsp
Lal mirch powder (Red chilli powder) 1 tbs or to taste

instructions: Combine the listed ingredients and mix well in a flat bowl.
Cover and marinate for 2 hours.
Combine cooking oil, heat it in a flat bottom pan.
Add the listed ingredients and mix well, fry over medium heat, until light golden, take out fried onion and remove excess oil reserve.
Combine the listed ingredients and grind well in a grinder.
Take out cover, Add ground paste, yogurt, coriander powder, kashmiri red chilli powder, cumin powder, red chilli powder, cooking oil, mix well.
Cover and marinate for 4-5 hours.

variants.name: Bihari Boti — Karachi's Partition Kebab

ingredients.text: 2 tbsp Safed Khus Khus (White Poppy Seeds)
1 tsp Sabut Garam Masala (Whole Spice Powder)

instructions: Soak 2 tablespoons of white khus khus (poppy seeds) in 4 tablespoons of warm water for 30 minutes. and then blend or grind in a small grinder with the soaking water until you get a smooth, milky paste.

In a large bartan (bowl), whisk together: mustard oil, raw papaya paste, poppy seed paste, besan, ginger-garlic paste, yoghurt, mace, nutmeg, red chilli powder, garam masala, and salt. Whisk well until the besan is fully incorporated — no lumps. The marinade will be quite thick and slightly orange-brown.
Stir in the pounded beef strips to the marinade and turn each piece to coat thoroughly. Cover the bartan with cling film and refrigerate for a minimum of 8 hours — 12-16 hours is ideal.
Remove marinated meat from the fridge 20 minutes before grilling — cold meat on hot grill seizes up.

Cook over a hot charcoal mangal (grill) or cast iron grill pan on maximum heat. Bihari kebab needs HIGH, fast heat — Aim for the outside to char slightly while the inside stays juicy. Grill for 3-4 minutes per side.
Warm a walnut-sized piece of hardwood charcoal until glowing orange, drop it in the katori, drizzle with ghee, and seal the lid immediately.

variants.name: Bihari Malai Boti

instructions: Combine cumin seeds, poppy seeds, coriander seeds, kabab cheeni, black pepper powder, green cardamom, cloves, cinnamon stick, mace, black cardamom, roasted grams, nutmeg, dry roast over low heat until fragrant in a pan.
Leave to cool down completely and move the mixture to a grinder.
Add, kashmiri red chilli powder, pink salt, fried onion, grind well, bihari malai boti spice combine is complete, reserve.
In a bowl, incorporate the prepared bihari malai boti spice combine, ginger garlic paste, cream, thick yogurt, mustard oil, lemon juice, whisk well.
Add boneless beef, papaya paste, mix well, cover and marinate for 6-8 hours or overnight.
Take out cover, thread 6-7 bihari malai beef boti on a skewer. (Makes 6-7 skewer).
Proceed by grill on charcoal for 8-10 minutes by moving the skewer, brush oil in between.
Serve with puri paratha, onion rings, raita and salad!

variants.name: Afghani Biryani (Ruz Bukhari)

ingredients.item: or 1 tbsp Zafran (Saffron) or Gulab Jal
ingredients.text: 1 pinch or 1 tbsp Zafran (Saffron) or Gulab Jal (Rose Water)

instructions: This step can be done first and kept warm — it will hold for hours. Heat 2 tablespoons of ghee in a frying pan over medium heat. Stir in the julienned carrots.

Warm 3 tablespoons of ghee in a large heavy-bottomed degh (pot) over medium heat. Stir in the sliced onions. Cook, stirring, for 12-15 minutes until golden (not dark brown like birista — just golden and soft).
Stir in the meat pieces to the pot with the spiced onions. Stir to coat in the ghee and spices. Cook on medium-high heat for 5 minutes, turning the meat.

Strain the remaining creamy broth — have about 1 cup of fragrant, milky stock. This stock will be used to cook the rice (instead of plain water) to infuse it with the char masala flavour from the inside.

In a large pot, bring 3 litres of salted water to a rolling boil. Drain the soaked rice and cook for 5-6 minutes until 65% done — the grain should bend but snap if you press it firmly. Drain through a colander.
In the same degh or a fresh heavy pot, layer as follows. Bottom layer: spread the cooked meat pieces evenly. Middle layer: spread the parboiled rice.
Put the pot on high heat for 3 minutes until you hear vigorous steaming. Reduce to minimum heat. Put a tawa (flat griddle) or folded cloth between the pot and flame as a heat diffuser.
Scatter the caramelized carrot-raisin-almond garnish generously over the entire surface. The garnish provides all the contrast and complexity.

variants.name: Authentic Karachi Biryani
instructions: Warm 4 tbsp tel (oil) in a deep karahi (wok) or pateela (pot) until a small piece of onion dropped in sizzles immediately (about 30 seconds to float back up). Stir in the onions in batches — don't overcrowd or they'll steam instead of Cook. Stir every 30.

In a large bowl, Mix the mutton pieces with dahi (yoghurt), biryani masala, adrak lehsan paste (ginger-garlic paste), half the barista pyaz (fried onions), and 1 tsp namak (salt). Cover with cling film and refrigerate for at least 2 hours.

Stir in the kharay masalay (whole spices: tej patta, elaichi, dalchini, laung) and enough namak so the water tastes like the sea. Bring to a rolling boil. Stir in the soaked and drained basmati chawal.

In the same degh (or a separate karahi), heat 3 tbsp tel (oil) on medium-high. Stir in the halved, peeled aloo. Cook them on each side for about 3-4 minutes until they're golden all over — you're not cooking them through, just building a crust that'll hold up.

In the same degh, Stir in the marinated gosht (meat) along with all the marinade. Turn the heat to high and bhunno (stir-Cook) for 10 minutes — hear aggressive sizzling, and the tamatar should start breaking down. and then reduce heat to low, cover with a tight lid.

Spread a layer of pudina (mint) leaves and hara dhaniya (coriander). gently spoon the parboiled chawal (rice) on top in an even layer — use a chamcha (ladle) and don't press down or you'll crush the grains.
Cook on the lowest possible flame for 25-30 minutes. Every peek releases steam and adds 5 minutes to the cooking time.

Turn off the heat but DO NOT open the lid yet. Let the biryani rest for 10 minutes — the residual steam finishes the cooking and lets the flavours settle. Try to keep the layers somewhat intact — this isn't a stir-Cook.

variants.name: Authentic Pakistani Chicken Biryani SIMPLIFIED!

ingredients.text: 1/2 tbsp bhunna zeera (roasted cumin powder) (can sub with cumin seeds)

ingredients.preparation: can sub with seeds, but try to dry roast first!
ingredients.text: 1 tbsp bhunna dhania (roasted coriander powder) (can sub with seeds, but try to dry roast first!)

ingredients.text: 1/8 tsp powdered mace (can sub with a small piece of mace )

ingredients.text: 3-5 green chilies cut long or in rounds

ingredients.item: food coloring dissolved in a 2 tbsp milk
ingredients.text: 1 tsp food coloring dissolved in a 2 tbsp milk

instructions: A small taste should give you a mix that's spicy and punchy! Marinate the chicken in the biryani masala, lemon juice, olive oil, yoghurt, and green chili paste for at least 30 minutes.

Warm 1/4 cup of oil in a large saute pan and Stir in your ginger and garlic pastes and cook on medium high heat until they no longer smell raw - about a minute. Stir in your diced tomatoes and cook, sauteing occasionally until the excess water dries and the oil rises above the tomatoes.

Stir in your marinated chicken, sauteing until the color changes. Stir in your potatoes, aloo bukharay (if using), half a cup of water, cover the pot, and bring it to a simmer, cooking for 25 minutes or so or until the chicken is tender. Check on it halfway through to see if the masala is sticking (Stir in.

When the chicken is tender, turn up the heat to dry out any excess water, turn the stove off as soon as it starts to stick a little and the oil is above the masala. Rinse your basmati rice until the water runs clear and soak it for at least 30 minutes.

10 minutes into the chicken cooking bring a big pot of water to boil with the salt, vinegar and flavorings. Once the water comes to a boil, drain and Stir in your rice, cook for 6.5-7.5 minutes until the rice is almost cooked through. Strain immediately.
Put half your rice at the bottom of the pot you used to cook it. Cover with the remaining rice.

Top with a few drops of kewra or biryani essence, drizzle over your rice coloring, and Stir in a few slices of lemon and/or tomatoes, extra cilantro over top and cover with a tightly fitting lid. Let it sit at the lowest heat on your stovetop for 20-25 minutes and and then carefully fluff and serve with raita and kachumbar.

alternate_methods.label: Alternate documented method
instructions: Mix chicken pieces with yogurt, adrak lehsan paste, and the entire biryani masala packet. Mix well so every piece is coated. Let it marinate while you prepare everything else — even 20 minutes makes a difference.
Warm oil in a karahi. Stir in 2 thinly sliced onions and Cook on medium-high heat, stirring regularly, until deep golden — about 15 minutes.

In the same oil, Stir in remaining sliced onion and soften. Stir in marinated chicken and tomatoes. Cook on high heat 5 minutes, and then medium heat until chicken is cooked through and oil separates, about 15-18 minutes.
Boil well-salted water. Stir in soaked and drained basmati. Cook 6 minutes, no more.
Spread chicken masala in the pot. Stir in rice on top. Cover tightly (use a kitchen towel under the lid to seal).
Turn off heat, rest 8 minutes.

variants.name: Balochi Biryani

ingredients.text: 2 tbsp adrak lehsan paste (ginger garlic paste)
1 tsp lal mirch powder (red chilli powder)

instructions: In a heavy deg, heat ghee. Stir in cracked kali mirch, smoked badi elaichi, and other whole spices. Stir in sliced pyaz and cook until golden.
In a separate pan, Cook sliced onions in oil until golden (not dark). Remove and drain.
Boil salted water. Stir in soaked rice and cook 7 minutes to 70% done. Drain well.
Spread mutton masala in the deg. Stir in rice on top. Stir in a few drops of warm ghee.

variants.name: Biryani Rice (Plain Sela Chawal)

ingredients.text: 1 kg sela basmati chawal (parboiled basmati rice)

instructions: Wash sela rice under cold running water 3-4 times until the water runs clear. Soak in cold water for 30 minutes.
In the largest pot you have, bring 4 litres of water to a rolling boil. Stir in salt, vinegar, oil, and whole spices.
Stir in soaked, drained sela rice to the boiling water. Stir immediately once to prevent sticking. Set a timer for 8 minutes from when the rice goes in.
The moment the rice reaches 70%, drain immediately through a large colander. Spread on a flat tray or the colander and let it steam-dry for 3-4 minutes.

Once steam-dried, the parboiled sela rice is ready to layer immediately for biryani. If not using right away, spread in a single layer on a tray and let cool completely before handling — warm parboiled rice can continue to cook from its own steam and become too soft.

variants.name: Biryani with Yogurt Marination

ingredients.text: 2 tbsp adrak lehsan paste (ginger garlic paste)
2 tsp lal mirch powder (red chilli powder)

ingredients.item: standard quantities zarda colour, kewra water, podina
ingredients.text: standard quantities zarda colour, kewra water, podina

instructions: In a large bowl, whisk yogurt smooth. Stir in adrak lehsan paste, lal mirch (1 tsp), dhania powder, haldi, garam masala, nimbu ras, 2 slit hari mirch, and salt. Stir in chicken pieces and mix until every surface is coated.
Take the marinated chicken out of the fridge 30 minutes before cooking.
Cook thinly sliced onions in oil/ghee to deep golden birista. In the same oil, Stir in remaining onion, soften, Stir in blended tomatoes, remaining 1 tsp lal mirch, and cook until oil rises.

Stir in the marinated chicken (along with all the yogurt clinging to it) to the masala. Cook on high heat 5 minutes, and then medium. The yogurt masala will cook down into a thick, flavourful coating on the chicken.
Parboil soaked basmati 6 minutes. Drain. Layer chicken masala in pot, Stir in rice in two layers with birista, colour, mint, and kewra.
Rest 10 minutes after dum.

variants.name: Bombay Biryani (Pakistani Style)

ingredients.text: 1 set Kharay Masalay (Whole Spices for rice water)

instructions: Warm 4 tablespoons of ghee or oil in a karahi over medium-high heat. Stir in the thinly sliced onions. Cook, stirring frequently, for 20-25 minutes until they turn a deep golden-amber colour and become crispy.
In the same ghee remaining in the karahi, Stir in the halved potatoes. Cook on medium-high heat, turning occasionally, for 8-10 minutes until the outside is golden and sealed.
In the same karahi, Stir in the meat pieces and stir over high heat for 3-4 minutes to colour the outside. Stir in the yoghurt and biryani masala. Stir well.

Stir in enough water to just cover the meat (about 1 cup for chicken, 2 cups for mutton). Cover the karahi and cook on low-medium heat until the meat is tender — chicken takes 20-25 minutes, mutton takes 45-60 minutes. If it looks too liquidy with 10 minutes.

In a large degh (pot) or separate pot, bring 3 litres of heavily salted water to a rolling boil (it should taste like mild seawater). Stir in the whole spices. Drain the soaked rice and Stir in to the boiling water.
In a large degh or pot, create layers. First, spread the meat masala as the bottom layer — scrape every last bit of sauce from the karahi. spread the parboiled rice over the top in an even layer.

Put the pot over high heat for 3 minutes until you hear active bubbling and see steam escaping. Reduce heat to the absolute minimum your stove can produce. Put a folded kitchen towel or thick tawa (griddle) between the pot and the flame — this creates a heat.
After 25 minutes, remove from heat.

variants.name: Craveworthy EASY Beef Biryani

ingredients.text: 2 medium potatoes cut into 1.5 inch pieces

ingredients.item: Juice of a lemon or lemon slices
ingredients.text: Juice of a lemon or lemon slices

ingredients.item: of yogurt mixed with 2 tbsp water
ingredients.text: 1 tsp of yogurt mixed with 2 tbsp water

instructions: Wash rice to drain away excess starch and and then soak and set aside. Boil the rice in salted water when your potatoes are just done so that the rice is still warm when you layer it. Warm 1/2 cup oil in saute mode instant pot and Stir in your whole spices.

When they sputter and smell toasty Stir in your onion and green chilies and cook till the edges of the onion are golden. Stir in your ginger and garlic paste, saute for a minute. Stir in the spices, give it a quick mix.

Stir in the beef, sauteeing until the beef cubes are evenly browned. Stir in your tomatoes, dried plums (if using), and 1.5 cup of hot water. Pressure cook (manual) for 15 minutes, the meat should be cooked through, but not tender.

Quick release and then Stir in the potatoes and put it back to pressure for 4 minutes. Taste and adjust seasoning - Aim for a little salty and a little spicy - if you have not used dried plums Stir in lemon juice at this point along with your garam masala, half your mint, cilantro, chilies. Warm 1/2 cup oil in a.

When they sputter and smell toasty Stir in your onion and green chilies and cook till the edges of the onion are golden. Stir in your ginger and garlic paste, sauté for a minute. Stir in your spices and cook for another minute.

Stir in in your meat cubes, sautéing until the beef cubes are evenly browned. Stir in your tomatoes, dried plums (if using), and 2 cup of hot water and let the mix simmer on low until the meat is cooked through but not tender, typically 45-50 minutes. Stir in in your potatoes and simmer till they're cooked through.

Cook until the excess water dries out and the masala starts sticking to the bottom. Stir in half your mint, half your cilantro, half your chilies, your garam masala and lemon (if using). Layer half the rice in the pot you used to cook it, and then the meat masala, and then scatter remaining cilantro, mint and chilies over top and follow.

Mix a little food color with yogurt and drizzle over top. Cover the pot and cook on the lowest heat for 25 minutes. Use a flat spoon or a small plate and gently mix it to avoid breaking the rice and serve with raita and kachumbar.

variants.name: Hyderabadi Biryani
instructions: Start the marinade (minimum 4 hours before cooking — overnight is ideal). In a large bowl, Stir in your gosht (mutton) pieces. Pour in the whisked dahi (yoghurt), adrak-lehsan (ginger-garlic) paste, biryani masala, lal mirch (red chilli powder), and a generous 1.5 tsp namak (salt).

Bring a large pateela (pot) of water to a rolling boil — use at least 8 cups. Stir in all your saabut masalay (whole spices): tej patta (bay leaves), badi elaichi (black cardamom), choti elaichi (green cardamom), dalchini (cinnamon), laung (cloves), javitri (mace). Stir in enough namak (salt).

Cook the aloo (potatoes). While your rice soaks or boils, heat about 1 cup of oil in a karahi (wok) or deep pan over medium-high heat. Stir in the halved, peeled potatoes and Cook for about 8-10 minutes, turning occasionally, until they're deep golden all over.

Spread the RAW marinated gosht in an even layer across the bottom. Do NOT pre-cook the meat — this is kacchi biryani, and the whole point is that the meat cooks in the dum steam. Put the fried aloo on top of the meat, cut-side down.

Stir in the chawal (rice) layer. Gently spoon the parboiled rice over the meat and potato layer, spreading it evenly. Finally, pour 2-3 tablespoons of water gently down the SIDES of the pot (not over the rice).

Put the sealed degh on HIGH heat for exactly 8-10 minutes. comes the patience: reduce to the LOWEST possible flame your stove can manage. If you have a cast-iron tawa (flat griddle pan), Put it between the burner and the pot — this diffuses the heat beautifully and.

Turn off the heat completely. Let the pot sit, still sealed, for 15 minutes — this resting period lets the steam redistribute and the layers settle. Aim for some mixing, but also visible streaks of zafrani (saffron) rice, white rice, and masala-stained rice from the meat layer.

variants.name: Karachi Beef Biryani

ingredients.text: 3 tbsp adrak lehsan paste (ginger garlic paste)
2.5 tsp lal mirch powder (red chilli powder)
1 cup podina aur dhania (mint and fresh coriander)
3 tbsp zarda rang dissolved in milk (food colour in milk)

instructions: Beef needs time that chicken doesn't. In a pressure cooker, Stir in beef pieces with 2 cups water, 1 tsp adrak lehsan paste, 1 tsp salt, and 3 sabut garam masala pieces (bay leaf, cardamom, cloves). Pressure cook for 25-30 minutes after the first whistle, or simmer covered.
In a wide karahi, heat ghee over medium-high. Stir in thinly sliced onions (4 large) and Cook, stirring regularly, until they turn deep golden-brown. This takes a patient 18-20 minutes.

In the same ghee-rich karahi, Stir in remaining sliced onion and cook until soft. Stir in adrak lehsan paste and bhuno (Cook) for 2 minutes until raw smell disappears. Stir in blended tomatoes and cook until oil rises, about 10 minutes.

Bring a large pot of water to a rolling boil. Stir in leftover beef stock (top up with plain water as needed), salt generously, and a few whole spices. Stir in soaked sela rice and cook 8-9 minutes — sela rice takes slightly longer than regular basmati.

In a heavy-bottomed deg or pot, start with the beef masala spread across the bottom. Stir in a layer of half the rice. Stir in remaining rice, top with remaining herbs, yellow colour in milk, and remaining birista.
Seal the pot with a tightly fitted lid (use dough rope if you have it) and Put on a tawa (flat griddle) over the lowest heat setting. Cook for 25-30 minutes.
After 30 minutes on dum, turn off heat and rest for 10 minutes. Use a large, flat spatula to gently turn the biryani from the edges inward in large folds — never stir vigorously.

variants.name: Karachi Prawn Biryani

ingredients.text: 2 tbsp adrak lehsan paste (ginger garlic paste)
1.5 tsp lal mirch powder (red chilli powder)
2 tbsp food colour dissolved in milk

instructions: Let them sit 10 minutes.
Warm oil in a karahi. Stir in thinly sliced onions and Cook until golden-brown, stirring regularly, about 15 minutes. Remove and drain.
In the same oil, Stir in sliced onion and cook until soft. Stir in adrak lehsan paste and Cook 1-2 minutes. Stir in blended tomatoes, lal mirch, salt, and cook until oil rises, about 8-10 minutes.
Boil well-salted water with a few whole spices. Stir in soaked basmati and cook 6 minutes to 70% done. Drain immediately.
Spread prawn masala in the pot. Stir in half the rice, scatter mint and coriander, drizzle colour and kewra, Stir in half the birista. Stir in remaining rice and repeat toppings.
Prawn biryani is at its absolute best the moment it comes off the heat. Garnish with a squeeze of fresh nimbu and a few sprigs of dhania.

variants.name: Kofta Biryani

ingredients.text: 2 tbsp adrak lehsan paste (ginger garlic paste)
2 tsp lal mirch powder (red chilli powder)

instructions: In a large bowl, Mix qeema with grated onion (squeezed to remove excess water), 1 tbsp adrak lehsan paste, chopped hari mirch, 1 tsp lal mirch, 1 tsp dhania powder, salt, anda, and besan. Mix thoroughly with your hands for 3-4 minutes until the mixture is smooth and.
Warm 2 tbsp oil in a flat pan. Stir in koftas in a single layer and cook on medium heat, turning every 2-3 minutes, until browned all over — about 10 minutes.

In the same ghee, Stir in remaining adrak lehsan paste, blended tomatoes, yogurt, remaining spices, and salt. Cook until oil rises and masala is thick, about 15 minutes. Simmer on low heat for 12-15 minutes.
Boil well-salted water. Stir in soaked basmati and cook 6-7 minutes. Drain.

In a wide, flat-bottomed pot, spread the kofta masala with all the koftas arranged evenly. Stir in rice in two layers with birista, colour, and herbs between and on top. Seal and dum on tawa on lowest heat for 22-25 minutes.

alternate_methods.label: Food Fusion alternate method — Kofta Biryani
instructions: Koftay (Meatballs): In chopper,Add beef mince,onion,coriander,green chilies,ginger garlic paste,cumin powder,salt,red chili powder,whole spice powder,bread slice and chop until well combined.
Proceed by grease your hands with oil,take a mixture and make 12-15 meat balls/koftya of equal sizes.
In frying pan,Add oil and fry meat balls/koftay for 2 minutes; reserve.
Biryani: In pot,Add ghee and let it melt,Add black pepper corns,cloves,cinnamon stick,green cardamom,black cardamom and cumin seeds,mix well.
Proceed by add onion and fry until light brown.
Proceed by add tomatoes and ginger garlic paste and mix well.
Add the listed ingredients and mix well.
Add yogurt,mix well; cook over high heat until oil separates.
Add the listed ingredients; cover; cook for 15-20 minutes over low heat.
Serve the finished Kofta biryani while fresh.

variants.name: KP Dum Biryani

ingredients.text: 1.2 kg mutton ya beef gosht (mutton or beef)
3 tbsp adrak lehsan paste (ginger garlic paste)
1.5 tsp lal mirch powder (red chilli powder)

ingredients.preparation: whole wheat flour for dough seal
ingredients.text: 300 g atta (whole wheat flour for dough seal)

instructions: Mix gosht with yogurt, adrak lehsan paste, half the crushed birista, all ground spices, and salt. Cover and refrigerate overnight.
Mix atta with just enough water to make a stiff, workable dough. Roll into a long rope about 2cm thick.
Cook onions in generous ghee to deep golden birista. Remove and drain. In the same ghee, Stir in whole spices, cook marinated gosht on high heat 8 minutes, and then Stir in chopped tomatoes.
Bring well-salted water to a rolling boil. Stir in soaked basmati and cook exactly 6-7 minutes. Drain and spread to cool slightly.
In a heavy deg, spread gosht masala. Layer rice in two portions with mint, birista, and kewra between layers and on top.
Put the sealed pot on a tawa over the absolute lowest heat possible. Cook for 35-40 minutes.
Use a knife to cut around the dough seal.

variants.name: Lahori Biryani

ingredients.text: 1 tsp Lal Mirch Powder (Red Chilli Powder)

instructions: Mix the yoghurt, ginger-garlic paste, biryani masala, red chilli powder, and 1 teaspoon salt in a large bowl. Whisk until smooth. Stir in the meat pieces and coat thoroughly.

The next day, heat 3 tablespoons of ghee in a karahi over medium heat. Stir in the thinly sliced onions. Cook, stirring frequently, for 20-25 minutes until deep golden brown and crispy — this takes patience.

In the same karahi with the reserved ghee (Stir in 2 more tablespoons if needed), Stir in ALL the whole spices at once over medium heat. Cook for 1 minute, stirring — they should sizzle and release fragrance. Stir in the marinated meat (all the yoghurt marinade comes.

Stir in 1 cup of hot water to the masala. Stir in half the birista and stir through. Cover the karahi and cook on low heat for 40-50 minutes for mutton, stirring every 10 minutes and adding a splash more water if it sticks, until the meat is.

In a large degh (pot), bring 3 litres of heavily salted water to a rolling boil. Stir in a few whole spices (bay leaf, cardamom, cloves) to the water. Drain the soaked rice and lower it into the boiling water.
In a large heavy-bottomed degh or pot, spread the cooked meat masala as the base layer. Spread the parboiled rice in an even layer on top. the other two Stir in invisible fragrance.

Put the pot over high heat for 3-4 minutes until steam builds and you hear active bubbling. Reduce to the absolute minimum heat setting. Put a folded kitchen towel or a flat tawa (griddle) under the pot as a heat diffuser.

Use a large flat spatula or a gentle folding technique to mix the layers partially — Aim for some of the bottom masala folding up through the rice but you don't want to break the grains or make it a uniform mush.

variants.name: Lahori Chicken Biryani

ingredients.text: 2 tbsp adrak lehsan paste (ginger garlic paste)
2 tsp lal mirch powder (red chilli powder)
6 tbsp ghee ya tail (ghee or oil)

instructions: Warm ghee or oil in a karahi (wok) over medium-high heat. Stir in all the onions at once.

In a large bowl, Mix chicken pieces with dahi (yogurt), adrak lehsan paste, lal mirch powder, haldi, 1 tsp garam masala powder, salt, and half the birista (crush it in your palm before adding). Mix well so every piece is coated.

In the same karahi with the reserved oil, Stir in sabut garam masala (whole spices) and let them splutter for 30 seconds. Stir in the marinated chicken and cook on high heat for 5 minutes, stirring constantly. Stir in chopped tamatar and cook until oil separates and rises.

Bring a large deg (pot) of heavily salted water to a rolling boil. Stir in soaked and drained basmati. Cook on high heat for exactly 6-7 minutes — the grains should be 70% cooked (they'll bend slightly but still have a firm white centre when you bite one).
In a heavy-bottomed deg (pot), layer as follows — first, spread all the chicken masala evenly. Next, Stir in half the partially cooked rice in an even layer. Stir in the rest of the rice.

Cover the pot tightly. Lahori cooks use atta (dough) to seal the lid for a perfect steam seal — roll a thick rope of dough and press it around the rim. Put the pot on a tawa (flat griddle) over the lowest possible heat.
Turn off the heat and let the biryani rest, still sealed, for 10 minutes.

variants.name: Leftover Curry Biryani - Transform Last Night's Curry Into a Fancy Dinner!
instructions: Prepare the white basmati rice; combine it with the yogurt, aromatics and measured spices, then allow the mixture to marinate.
Rinse and soak the rice. Boil it in salted water with the whole spices until about three-quarters cooked, then drain.
Cook the marinated mixture until the protein is tender and the masala is thick rather than watery.
Layer the masala and rice, add the reserved herbs and aromatics, cover tightly and finish over very low heat until the rice is tender.
Rest the covered pot for 10 minutes, then lift the rice gently from the bottom to serve.

variants.name: Multani Biryani

ingredients.text: 2.5 tbsp adrak lehsan paste (ginger garlic paste)
1.5 tsp lal mirch powder (red chilli powder)

instructions: Mix mutton with yogurt, adrak lehsan paste, lal mirch, garam masala, salt, and half the birista. Stir in soaked khubani (apricots) halved. Marinate minimum 3 hours, overnight preferred.
Warm ghee in a large karahi. Cook all sliced onions until very deep golden, 20-22 minutes. Remove, drain, and set aside.

In the reserved ghee, cook the marinated mutton on high heat for 8-10 minutes. Reduce heat, cover, and cook for 50-60 minutes until mutton is very tender, stirring occasionally. Stir in kishmish in the final 10 minutes.
Boil generously salted water. Stir in a few whole spices, the mint stalks, and soaked basmati. Parboil 7-8 minutes to 70% done.
Spread mutton masala in the pot. Stir in half the rice. Stir in remaining rice and repeat toppings generously.
Seal tightly and cook on tawa on lowest heat for 30-35 minutes. Rest 15 minutes before opening. Fold gently and garnish with remaining dry fruits and a final drizzle of warm ghee.

variants.name: Pakistani Prawn Biryani Recipe (Shrimp Biryani)

ingredients.preparation: washed in several changes of water
ingredients.text: 2 1/2 cups basmati rice (washed in several changes of water)
1 pound prawns or shrimp (peeled and tails removed)
1 medium yellow onion (halved and thinly sliced)

ingredients.item: bird's eye chilies or 1 serrano pepper
ingredients.text: 2 bird's eye chilies or 1 serrano pepper (finely chopped)

instructions: Bring a large pot of water (at least 4 quarts) to a rolling boil. Reduce to a simmer and Stir in the green and black cardamom, cinnamon stick, bay leaves, and about 1 tablespoon of salt. Stir in the rice and cook on low heat for no more than 5 to 7 minutes. Once parboiled, drain immediately into a colander and set.

Warm oil over medium-low heat in a heavy-bottomed stockpot. Once it shimmers, Stir in the onions and cook for 10 to 15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until evenly golden brown. Stir in the crushed ginger and garlic and stir for about 30 seconds until the raw smell cooks off.

Stir in the cumin powder, coriander powder, red chili flakes, and turmeric powder. Stir for 1 to 2 minutes until the spices are fragrant. Increase the heat and Stir in the chopped tomatoes. Stir continuously until they soften and break down, about 5 to 7 minutes.

Stir in the prawns and cook on high heat for 3 to 5 minutes until opaque and just cooked through. Stir in the chopped green chili and cilantro. Remove from heat. Transfer half the masala to a separate bowl.

In a separate stockpot, Stir in half the cooked rice. Spoon the reserved prawn masala over the rice, and then cover with the remaining rice. Pour the rest of the saffron liquid over the top and stir very gently without disturbing the masala layer.

To put the biryani on dum, turn the heat to high briefly, and then reduce to the lowest setting. Wrap the lid tightly with a cotton cloth and cover the pot. Steam for 10 minutes. Transfer to a large serving platter and garnish with fresh cilantro and green chilies.

variants.name: Pakistani Punjabi Biryani

ingredients.item: Generous handfuls of chopped fresh coriander/cilantro + mint leaves
ingredients.text: Generous handfuls of chopped fresh coriander/cilantro + mint leaves
Optional: Yellow food coloring (a piece of coal.)

instructions: Slice your onions and cook in oil in a large pot till browned.
Put in the ginger, garlic and tomatoes and cook till mushy.
Stir in the yogurt, remaining spices, meat, green chillies and mix well.
If cooking chicken and then Stir in one cup of hot water, bring to a boil and then simmer till tender. beef and mutton Stir in more water.
Stir in coriander leaves and mint leaves.
In large pot Stir in water, salt, vinegar to the soaked rice and boil till it is parboiled i.e.
Strain the rice when done.
Layer the rice in the following order: half the rice, all the meat masala, remaining rice, sprinkle over the yellow food coloring, and leave on the lowest heat setting for 15-20 minutes.
You can do this after your biryani is ready or Stir in it before your set the biryani over low heat for 20 minutes.

variants.name: Pakistani Vegetable Biryani

ingredients.text: 1.5 tbsp adrak lehsan paste (ginger garlic paste)
2 tbsp zarda colour in milk (food colour in milk)

instructions: Make your fried onions first — thin-sliced pyaz fried in oil over medium heat for 15-18 minutes until deep golden. Drain and set aside.
In the birista oil, Stir in remaining sliced onion and soften. Stir in adrak lehsan paste and Cook 1-2 minutes. Stir in blended tomatoes, all spices, and salt.
Boil salted water with whole spices, Stir in soaked basmati and cook 6 minutes to 70% done. Drain.
Spread vegetable masala in the pot. Stir in rice in two layers with mint, birista, colour, and kewra between and on top. Seal tightly and dum on tawa on low heat for 18-20 minutes.
Rest 5 minutes after turning off heat.
After dum, rest 5 minutes before opening.

variants.name: Peshawari Biryani

ingredients.text: 1 kg mutton ya murgh (mutton or chicken)
2 tbsp adrak lehsan paste (ginger garlic paste)
1 tsp lal mirch powder (red chilli powder)

instructions: In a heavy karahi, heat ghee over medium-high heat. Stir in the sabut garam masala — the black cardamom, cinnamon, green cardamom, and cloves. Stir in sliced onions and cook until golden.

Once the meat is added, cook on high heat for 5 minutes and then reduce to medium-low. Cover and cook, stirring every 10 minutes, for 40-50 minutes until the mutton is completely tender and the masala has reduced to a thick coat.
In a small pan, heat 1 tbsp ghee. Stir in blanched badam (almond) slices and toast until golden, about 2 minutes. Stir in kishmish (raisins) and stir for 30 seconds until they puff up.
Boil a large pot of well-salted water. Stir in kali zeera (black cumin) and a few whole spices to the water. Stir in soaked basmati and parboil 6-7 minutes to 70% done.
In a heavy pot, spread the cooked gosht masala. Stir in parboiled rice on top. Seal tightly and cook on a tawa on lowest heat for 20-25 minutes.
Open the pot, gently fold the rice and meat together. Transfer to a large serving platter.

variants.name: Sindhi Biryani

ingredients.text: 1 set Kharay Masalay (Whole Spices for Rice)
1 bunch each Pudina aur Dhaniya (Mint and Coriander)

instructions: Mix meat pieces with dahi (yoghurt), half the barista pyaz (fried onions), adrak lehsan paste (ginger-garlic paste), Sindhi biryani masala, and salt. Marinate for minimum 3 hours — overnight in the fridge is ideal.

Warm 3 tbsp tel (oil) in a heavy degh (pot) on high heat. Cook the halved aloo (potatoes) on both cut sides until golden — about 3-4 minutes per side. This crust prevents them from breaking apart during the slow cook in the masala.
In the same degh, Stir in the marinated meat with all its marinade. Turn heat to high. Stir in the chopped tamatar (tomatoes) and all the hari mirch (green chillies).
Bring a large degh of water to a rolling boil with kharay masalay (whole spices) and enough salt that the water tastes sea-salty. Stir in the soaked, drained basmati. Drain immediately.

Spread the meat and loose masala evenly across the bottom of the degh. Arrange the fried aloo halves prominently over the meat — they should be visible and numerous. Stir in a generous layer of pudina (mint) and hara dhaniya (coriander) — more than in Karachi biryani.
Seal the degh with foil pressed tight against the rim, and then Put the lid on top. Cook on the lowest possible heat for 25-30 minutes. Rest off heat, still sealed, for 10 minutes.

Add ginger garlic paste and mix well. In a remaining fried onion.
Proceed by add chicken and fry until chicken changes color.
Add the listed ingredients and mix well; cook for 4-5 minutes.
Proceed by add tomatoes and mix well.
Proceed by add green chilies,plums,green coriander,mint leaves and mix well.
Cover; cook for 6-8 minutes.

Take out half quantity of cooked chicken and gravy; reserve,Add lemon juice,cooked rice,boiled potatoes, remaining cooked chicken,fried onion,lemon juice,remaining cooked rice,water,yellow food color,fried onion and drizzle oil,cover and steam cook for 10 minutes.

variants.name: Sindhi Lamb Biryani

ingredients.text: 1.1 lb lamb or mutton, bone in

ingredients.item: potatoes, peeled and chopped into chunks
ingredients.text: 9 oz potatoes, peeled and chopped into chunks

ingredients.item: a few pinches orange/yellow food colour
ingredients.text: a few pinches orange/yellow food colour

instructions: Prepare the garlic, minced; combine it with the yogurt, aromatics and measured spices, then allow the mixture to marinate.
Rinse and soak the rice. Boil it in salted water with the whole spices until about three-quarters cooked, then drain.
Cook the marinated mixture until the protein is tender and the masala is thick rather than watery.
Layer the masala and rice, add the reserved herbs and aromatics, cover tightly and finish over very low heat until the rice is tender.
Rest the covered pot for 10 minutes, then lift the rice gently from the bottom to serve.

variants.name: South Punjab Mutton Biryani

ingredients.text: 3 tbsp adrak lehsan paste (ginger garlic paste)
2 tsp lal mirch powder (red chilli powder)

instructions: Mix mutton with yogurt, adrak lehsan paste, lal mirch, dhania powder, 1 tsp garam masala, salt, and half the crushed birista. Cover and marinate in the fridge overnight — minimum 4 hours if pressed for time.
Warm ghee in a large karahi. Stir in all 5 sliced onions at once. This is a large batch and will take 20-25 minutes to reach the right deep-brown colour.
In a large, heavy deg with the birista ghee, Stir in the marinated mutton. Cook on high heat for 8-10 minutes, stirring to prevent sticking. Reduce to medium and Stir in chopped tomatoes.
Bring a very large pot of salted water to a boil. Stir in mint stalks, 2 cardamom pods, and 1 bay leaf to the water for fragrance. Stir in soaked basmati and parboil for 7-8 minutes.
In the same deg used for mutton, spread the cooked masala evenly. Stir in 1/3 of the rice. Stir in another 1/3 rice.

Seal the deg tightly. If using dough to seal: take 500g atta (flour), Stir in water to make a stiff dough, roll into a thick rope, press around the rim, and press the lid firmly on top. Cook on a tawa on the lowest heat for 30-35 minutes.
REST, REVEAL, AND REJOICE: After 35 minutes, turn off heat and rest for 15 minutes before opening.

variants.name: Turkey Biryani

ingredients.item: turkey breast cubed into 1 1/2 - 2 inch pieces
ingredients.text: 1 pound turkey breast cubed into 1 1/2 - 2 inch pieces

ingredients.item: potatoes peeled & sliced into 1 cm rounds
ingredients.text: 2 potatoes peeled & sliced into 1 cm rounds

instructions: Mix the ingredients for the marinade in a medium sized bowl, Stir in the turkey pieces and stir to coat well. Soak the rice and set aside. Warm a generous amount of oil in a heavy bottomed pot and Stir in the whole spices.

When they start to splutter and give of a heady aroma and then Stir in the onions. Caramelize the onions on medium heat, watching carefully to make sure they don’t burn. Turn the heat down a little and Stir in the ginger and garlic, sauté for a minute.

Put in all the spices (chilli powder, chilli flakes, coriander powder, turmeric, salt) and cook for another minute or so. Turn the heat up and cook stirring frequently until you can no longer see any raw patches. Stir in the dried plums + a cup of hot water and simmer for about 25-30 minutes.

While the turkey is cooking bring a pot of water to boil with the bay leaf and vinegar. Season generously with salt. When the water boils Stir in the rice & cook until it is al dente. Drain and set aside. After 25-30 minutes the turkey should be cooked through, but not quite tender.

In go your sliced potatoes, give the masala a good stir, Stir in more water if needed and cook for another 20 minutes. Once the potatoes are tender and then crank up the heat and make sure you cook the masala so that the oil rises above the spice base. You can tip the dish a little to drain extra oil at.

Layer half the cooked rice on the bottom of a large wide pot, followed by the turkey masala, the mint and cilantro leaves and the remaining rice. Scatter the yellow powder on top along with a few drops of kewra water and leave on low for 20 minutes.

variants.name: White Biryani

ingredients.text: 1 tsp green chili paste (or 2/3 minced green chilies)
1-2 small pieces of mace (or 1/4 tsp ground)

ingredients.item: a few drops of kewra essence
ingredients.text: a few drops of kewra essence

instructions: Mix the marinade ingredients in a bowl, Stir in the chicken and set aside for at least 30 minutes. Warm your pan/wok Stir in oil on medium high heat.
When the oil is hot, Stir in the cumin seeds and then the onions. Saute until the edges start to change color and and then immediately Stir in your marinated chicken.
Stir the chicken well, sautéing until it's all changed color. Stir in a splash of water, bring it to a simmer and then turn down the heat and cook for 20-25 minutes or until the chicken is tender.

Turn up the heat and dry up the masala, sauteing occasionally, until the oil rises above it, the masala starts to stick to the bottom just a little and the chicken takes on a lovey golden hue. Wash the rice well, rinsing till the water turns more or less clear, and soak for at least 30 minutes.
Put all the ingredients listed in the Potli/Rice Bundle category and set aside until ready to cook. Bring a large pot of salted water to boil with the potli in it.

Stir in the washed rice and cook until the grains of rice will break easily with a little pressure, but not become mushy. For me this is usually anywhere between 7-10 minutes. Drain the rice and remove the potli.
Stir in the mint, cilantro, and green chilies. Squeeze over a little lemon juice and Stir in a few drops of kewra. Steam on low heat for 20-25 minutes.

ingredients.item: Italian style eggplant or 2 small ones
ingredients.text: 1 large Italian style eggplant or 2 small ones (sliced crosswise, about 1/2-inch thick)
1 large yellow onion or 2 small ones (halved and thinly sliced)
1 teaspoon red chili powder (preferably Kashmiri red chili powder)

ingredients.item: full-fat yogurt preferably 1/4 of it will be sour yogurt
ingredients.text: 2 cups full-fat yogurt preferably 1/4 of it will be sour yogurt (lightly whisked)

instructions: In a frying pan, heat 1⁄2 cup of oil over medium heat. When it begins shimmer, Stir in the sliced eggplant in batches. Cook each side until a medium brown, 1 to 3 minutes.

In a large heavy-bottom pot, heat remaining (about 1⁄4 cup) of oil over medium-low heat. Stir in sliced onions and Cook until soft and translucent, about 7 minutes. Stir in 1⁄2 teaspoon of crushed garlic, and Cook for a few seconds until it stops smelling raw.
Stir in tomatoes, green chili, salt, turmeric and red chili powder. Stir until well-mixed. Cover the pot and let it simmer on medium-low heat for 5 minutes.
Dial heat to low, cover, and let it steam for 10 minutes.
While the eggplant steams, transfer yogurt to a flat serving dish and lightly whisk until it has an even consistency. Stir in 1 teaspoon of crushed garlic.
Carefully spoon the eggplant, tomato and onion mixture, and layer it on top of the whisked yogurt. Garnish with dried mint, red chili flakes and pomegranate seeds.

instructions: Drain your overnight-soaked chanay (chickpeas) and put them in a bari degh (large pot) with 6 cups of fresh water. Bring to a boil over high heat, and then reduce to medium and let them cook until tender — about 40-45 minutes in a regular pot, or 4-5. Do NOT drain them — you'll need about 1 cup of that gorgeous brown.

In a separate pateela (cooking pot), heat the tel (oil) over medium heat until it shimmers. Stir in the saabut zeera (whole cumin seeds). Immediately Stir in the chopped pyaz (onions) to the crackling zeera. Stir well to coat in the oil. Bhunno (Cook) the pyaz on medium heat, stirring every minute or so, until they turn golden brown — about 7-8.

Stir in the adrak-lehsan (ginger-garlic) paste to the browned pyaz. Bhunno (stir-Cook) for about 1 minute — Continue until the raw smell disappears and a rich, cooked garlic aroma hits you. Stir in the chopped tamatar (tomatoes), lal mirch (red chilli powder), haldi (turmeric), dhaniya (coriander) powder, and. Begins the bhunna (stir-frying) — the most important technique in Pakistani cooking. Cook this.

Stir in the boiled chanay to the masala, along with about 1 cup of their dark chai-infused cooking water. Stir well so every chickpea gets coated in that gorgeous masala. Stir in the chana masala and ground anardana (dried pomegranate). Stir to distribute evenly.

Reduce heat to low and let the channay simmer on dum (gentle steam) for 20-25 minutes, stirring every 5 minutes or so. The gravy should reduce and thicken until it clings to each chickpea like a thick coating. If it gets too thick, Stir in a splash of. Turn off the heat. Sprinkle garam masala over the top and stir gently —.

Knead the dough for 7–8 minutes — longer than for paratha. Push forward with the heel of your hand, fold back, turn 90 degrees, and repeat.
Cover the dough ball with a damp cloth or an inverted bowl and leave for 20–30 minutes minimum.
Roll each piece between your palms into a smooth ball with no cracks on the surface — cracks indicate the dough needs a touch more water or kneading.

Dust a dough ball lightly in dry flour and Put on your chakla (rolling board). Use your belan (rolling pin) to roll from the centre outward, applying even pressure. Roll until the chapati is about 20–22 cm across and thin enough that you can just see your hand.

COOK ON THE TAWA — FIRST STAGE: Heat your tawa (flat griddle pan) over medium-high heat for 2–3 minutes. Cook the second side for 30–45 seconds — see light golden-brown spots forming on the cooked side.
COOK ON THE FLAME — THE PUFF STAGE: This is the moment.

Transfer the puffed chapati to a roti basket or plate lined with a cloth. Cover to keep warm and repeat with remaining dough balls. Cook and serve in batches — chapati is best eaten within 5 minutes of coming off the flame.

instructions: Proceed by soak Pomegranate seeds in warm water for 10 minutes. Remove excess water and coarsely grind them.

Combine beef mince, soaked pomegranate seeds, whole spice powder, roasted gram flour, green chilies, salt, red chili flakes, coriander seeds, coriander leaves, onion, egg and butter. Mix well. Refrigerate mixture for 10-20 minutes in a bowl.
Before frying Add tomatoes, mix well. Make patty and Add a tomato slice on top and fry each side for 4-5 min over low heat until it done. Avoid turning sides in between.
Present chapli Kababs with Knorr Tomato Ketchup and Knorr chili Garlic Sauce.

variants.name: Bannu Chapli Kebab — The Original

ingredients.text: 4 tbsp Dumba fat or cooking oil

instructions: Mix minced beef with all ingredients: dried pomegranate seeds, coriander, tomato, onion, green chilies, ginger-garlic paste, crushed coriander seeds, cumin, salt, and egg. Mix with your hands for 3-4 minutes — really work it together until uniform and sticky.
Cover and refrigerate for 30 minutes minimum.
Take a handful of mixture (about 100g). The flat shape is the whole point: more surface area = more crust.
Warm oil or dumba fat in a wide, heavy pan on high heat until smoking. Stir in the chapli kebabs — don't crowd. Cook 4-5 minutes until the bottom is deeply crusted and brown.
Flip once (only once) and cook 3-4 minutes on the other side. The kebab should have a deep golden-brown, almost crispy crust on both sides. Don't fiddle — let the heat do the work.
Drain on paper towels for 1 minute.

variants.name: Beef Chapli Kebab

ingredients.text: 6 tbsp beef tallow ya tel (beef tallow or oil)

instructions: Cut tomato in half, squeeze out seeds and excess juice. Adding seeds makes chapli kebab too wet and the discs won't hold shape.
Mix all ingredients including the deseeded tomato pieces, pomegranate seeds, and crushed coriander. Mix firmly for 5-6 minutes.
Wet hands and press mixture into flat, round discs about 3-4 inches in diameter and 1/2 inch thick.
Warm beef tallow or oil in a flat pan on medium-high. Shallow-Cook chapli kebabs for 5-6 minutes per side. Do not crowd the pan — Cook 2-3 at a time for proper heat.
The top and bottom should be deep brown with the sides slightly crisper. Drain on paper and serve immediately.

variants.name: Chicken Chapli Kebab

ingredients.text: 500 g raan ka qeema (minced chicken thigh)
3 tbsp charbi ya makhan (fat or butter)
1.5 tbsp adrak lahsun paste (ginger garlic paste)

instructions: Mix minced butter or fat into the chicken mince first, before adding other ingredients.
Deseed and dry the tomato. Stir in all remaining ingredients to the fattened mince. Mix firmly for 5-6 minutes.
Refrigerate for 1 hour minimum. Chicken chapli mixture is softer than beef and needs the chill to firm up enough to shape and hold in the pan.
Shape into flat discs from cold mixture — work quickly.
Shallow Cook on medium heat (not high — chicken burns). 4-5 minutes per side. Don't increase heat trying to darken it or the inside will be raw.
Once the bottom is set and brown, they flip cleanly.

variants.name: Peshawari Chapli Kebab
instructions: Put the coarsely ground keema (beef mince) in a large bowl. Stir in the diced pyaz (onion), deseeded and diced tamatar (tomatoes), chopped hari mirch (green chillies), hara dhaniya (fresh coriander), crushed anardana (pomegranate seeds), crushed dhania saboot (coriander seeds), whole zeera (cumin seeds), anda (egg), makki ka.
Wet your hands — this prevents sticking.
Put a large tawa (flat griddle pan) or heavy frying pan over high heat. Stir in the charbi (bone marrow fat) or ghee. Let it heat until it's shimmering and almost smoking — see tiny wisps of smoke.

Carefully slide the patties into the hot charbi — use a flat spatula to lower them gently, laying them away from you (so any splatter goes the other direction). Cook for 3-4 minutes WITHOUT moving them. The bottom is forming a crispy, golden-brown crust.
Using a wide spatula, flip each kebab in one confident motion. Cook for another 3-4 minutes.
Stir in a dollop of hari chutney (green chutney) if you have it.

variants.name: Swat Chapli Kebab — Valley Mountain Version

ingredients.text: 1 tbsp Sabut dhania crushed (coriander seeds, crushed)

instructions: Mix keema with all ingredients until well combined.
Cover and refrigerate 30-60 minutes.
Swat chaplis are thicker than Bannu — shape oval patties about 1.5-2cm thick.
Unlike Bannu chaplis (which cook on very high heat for a thin crust), Swat chaplis need medium-high heat to cook through without burning the outside. Cook 5-6 minutes per side.

instructions: Mix atta, salt, and warm water into a soft, pliable dough. Knead 5-8 minutes until smooth. Rest covered for 20 minutes.
Mix raw minced beef with onion, coriander, green chili, cumin, black pepper, and 0.5 tsp salt. Don't cook the filling — it cooks inside the bread. Mix well.

In the final minute, Stir in a small knob of butter or ghee around the bread and let it sizzle and baste the bread as it finishes.

variants.name: Hunza Chapshuro

ingredients.text: 1 large handful Hara Dhania (Fresh Green Coriander)

instructions: In a large bartan (bowl), mix 2.5 cups of atta (whole wheat flour) with half a teaspoon of salt. Make a well in the centre and begin adding warm water gradually — start with half a cup, mix with your fingers in circular motions, and then keep adding.

In a bartan, Mix the minced qeema (beef or mutton), very finely chopped onion, chopped green coriander (dhania), finely chopped green chillies, half tsp black pepper, half tsp cumin, and half tsp salt. Mix thoroughly with your hands — really squeeze and press everything together for 2 minutes.

Divide the rested dough into 4 equal balls — each about the size of a small fist. On a lightly floured surface, roll one ball into a circle about 20-22cm in diameter (roughly the size of a dinner plate) and about 3-4mm thick.
Fold the empty half of the dough circle over the filled half to create a half-moon shape.

COOK ON THE TAWA — FIRST SIDE: Heat a large tawa (flat griddle) or heavy frying pan over medium heat. No oil needed for the first side — dry cook on the tawa first. Cook on medium heat for 4-5 minutes until the bottom is golden-brown with darker.
The cooked side should be beautifully golden-brown. Cook the second side for another 4-5 minutes until equally golden-brown.
Transfer the tawa-cooked Chapshuro to a baking tray and Put in a pre-heated oven at 180°C (350°F) for 8-10 minutes.

BRUSH, CUT, AND SERVE: Remove from the oven (or tawa) and immediately brush the top surface with a light coating of ghee or butter while still hot. Cut each Chapshuro into 3-4 wedges, like a pizza (hence the nickname).

instructions: Sprinkle the salt evenly over every surface of the chicken, including inside the slashes and under any loose skin.
Light your charcoal grill or a sigri (small coal grill) and let the charcoal burn until it is covered in a layer of grey-white ash and glowing orange underneath. This takes 20-30 minutes.
Alternatively, lay a few cubes of fat directly on the hot grill grate — they will render and drip onto the coals, which will smoke and flame up, creating that characteristic charsi flavour.
Put the chicken pieces on the hot grill, skin side down. Do not move them for 4-5 minutes. hear aggressive sizzling — if it's quiet, the grill isn't hot enough.
After 30-35 minutes total grilling time, check the thickest piece (usually the leg quarter). Alternatively, the internal temperature should read 75°C (165°F) if you have a meat thermometer.
Remove the chicken from the grill and let it rest on a plate for 5 minutes.

instructions: Warm a cm of oil in a saucepan or pot and Stir in your onions and minced green chili.
Saute on medium heat till the onions edges are a bronze colour, 6-7 minutes.
Stir in in the garlic and ginger, give it a quick stir.
Stir in your chicken, spices, and cook medium high stirring frequently until the chicken changes colour and the masala coats it. 3 minutes or so.

Stir in your tomatoes and yoghurt, stir and cover. Simmer on low heat till tender. 20 minutes for chicken thighs, if your chicken breast is tough at this point and then Stir in in a splash of water and simmer for an additional 10 minutes.
When the chicken is done and then crank the heat up to dry up the extra water and create a cohesive masala.
Adjust the consistency to your liking and Stir in in the kasuri methi, butter, and roasted cumin and coriander powders.
Check for seasoning, garnish and serve.

variants.name: Chicken Corn Soup (Pakistani Chinese Style)
instructions: Bring to a boil over high heat, and then reduce to a steady simmer. Skim off any grey foam that rises to the surface during the first 5-10 minutes — this is protein impurities and removing it gives you a clear, clean stock. Simmer for 25-30 minutes.

Once the chicken is cooked through and tender, remove it from the stock with tongs and set it on a board to cool for 5 minutes. Strain the stock through a sieve into a clean pot — discard the ginger and garlic.
Bring the strained stock back to a gentle boil. Stir in the sweet corn kernels and the shredded chicken. Stir in the light soy sauce and white pepper.

Mix 4 tbsp cornflour with 6 tbsp cold water until completely smooth — no lumps. Pour this slowly into the simmering soup while stirring continuously in one direction. Keep stirring as you pour, or you will get cornflour lumps instead of a smooth, thick soup.

Beat the eggs in a small bowl until the yolk and white are fully combined. Reduce the soup to a gentle simmer — it should be moving but not bubbling aggressively. Hold the bowl of beaten egg about 15cm above the soup and pour it in a thin.
Taste for final seasoning — more salt, more white pepper if needed. Ladle into individual bowls and garnish with sliced spring onions. Diners customise their own heat level.

instructions: Rub the chicken pieces with the spice mix and set aside. Warm your pan on medium heat, Stir in the oil and once it shimmers and then Stir in in your onion and green chili.
Stir in the ginger and garlic paste, cook for a minute to get the rawness out. Stir in in the tomatoes, kashmiri laal mirch, and 1/2 tsp salt.

Cook, covered for a few minutes to hasten the softening of the tomatoes. Uncover and cook on medium high heat to take out some of the excess moisture, when the masala comes together, it will be one cohesive delicious looking paste, and then remove it from the pan.

If your blender can handle high heat liquids and then you can puree it right away - otherwise wait for the mixture to cool a little. Stir in the chicken pieces to the pan on medium high heat and saute until the color changes completely.

Stir your pureed mix back into the pan, along with half a cup of water. Bring it to a simmer and and then let it cook, covered, and on low heat until the chicken is tender (20 minutes - more if needed). Stir in your cream to the handi and bring it to a gentle simmer.

This is when you can Stir in more spice (remaining kashmiri laal mirch), salt, some tomato paste, or even a pinch of sugar to balance out the flavours. Garnish with a drizzle of cream and your favorite toppings.

variants.name: Creamy Chicken Handi

ingredients.text: 1 tsp Lal Mirch Powder (Red Chilli Powder)

instructions: Put your handi (clay pot) or a heavy-bottomed karahi (wok) on medium heat. Stir in 3 tablespoons of tel (cooking oil) and let it heat until it shimmers — you'll see tiny ripples on the surface.
Stir in your sliced pyaz (onions) to the hot oil. Spread them out and let them cook on medium heat, stirring every 2-3 minutes. This takes 12-15 minutes.

Stir in the adrak lahsun paste (ginger-garlic paste) to the golden onions. Stir constantly for 60-90 seconds — it'll sizzle aggressively and turn darker. Stir in lal mirch powder, dhaniya powder, and haldi.

Tip in the chopped tamatar (tomatoes). Stir everything together and turn the heat to medium-high. Cook uncovered, stirring occasionally, until the tomatoes break down completely into a thick paste and you can see the tel (oil) separating and floating on the surface — about 12-15 minutes.

Stir in your chicken pieces to the masala and stir to coat every piece. Cook on high heat for 3-4 minutes, turning the pieces so they sear slightly and absorb the masala colour. lower the heat to medium and Stir in the dahi (yoghurt) — stir it in.
Stir in half a cup of paani (water), stir, and then cover the handi with a lid. Cook on low-medium heat for 20-25 minutes until the murgh (chicken) is completely cooked through.
Turn the heat down to the absolute lowest setting. Stir in the malai (cream) and stir gently. and then Stir in the makhan (butter) and let it melt into the curry.

Scatter chopped hara dhaniya (fresh coriander) over the top and Stir in a few slit hari mirchein (green chillies) if you like a little heat visible. Let the handi sit covered for 5 minutes off the heat — this resting time lets the cream fully absorb into the.

instructions: Blend 2 raw onions to smooth paste with a splash of water. Heat ghee in a handi or heavy pot. Stir in onion paste and cook on medium heat, stirring frequently, for 10-12 minutes until raw smell is completely gone and paste has turned slightly golden — but.

Stir in chicken pieces, salt. Bhuno on medium heat (not high — to maintain pale colour) for 6-7 minutes until chicken is white and firm on outside.
Reduce to low heat. Stir in whisked yogurt 1 tablespoon at a time, stirring constantly. Once all incorporated, cook on medium 8 minutes.
Stir in cashew paste, stir until smooth. Stir in 1/4 cup water. Cook covered on low-medium for 20 minutes until chicken is completely cooked and tender.
Stir in fresh cream. Stir gently and cook 5 minutes on low — don't boil after adding cream. Stir in kewra water off-heat.
Garnish with light hara dhania and julienned ginger.

variants.name: Desi Dhaba Handi
