instructions: For the best meethi lassi, your dahi (yoghurt) and bartan (bowl) should be cold before you start. Put the yoghurt in the freezer for 15 minutes if it's not fridge-cold.

Stir in dahi (yoghurt), cold pani (water) or ice cubes, cheeni (sugar), and freshly ground elaichi (cardamom) to a blender. Blend on high speed for 60-90 seconds until completely smooth, frothy, and slightly aerated.
If using gulab jal (rose water), stir it in by hand — do not blend it. A gentle stir keeps the aroma concentrated.
Pour the lassi into tall, chilled glasses — fill to about 2cm from the top.

Sprinkle crushed pista (pistachios) over the malai. If feeling extravagant, Stir in a tiny pinch of saffron strands. Serve immediately with a long spoon or a straw — the traditional way is to stir the malai into the lassi yourself at the table, getting a bit of cream.

variants.name: Makki Ki Roti

ingredients.text: 2 cups makki ka atta (stone-ground cornmeal / coarse corn flour)
3 tablespoons ghee ya makhan (ghee or white butter)

instructions: We shape it differently, and that's part of its charm.
In a large bowl, Mix the makki ka atta and salt. Stir in warm water a little at a time, mixing as you go. Aim for dough that holds its shape when pressed but doesn't crumble.

Put your tawa (flat griddle pan) on the stove over medium-low heat. Let it heat up while you shape the rotis. This bread cooks on lower heat than chapati — lower and slower gives it time to cook through without burning the outside.
SHAPE THE ROTI — METHOD 1 (WET HANDS): Divide the dough into 4–6 equal balls.
SHAPE THE ROTI — METHOD 2 (PLASTIC WRAP): Tear two pieces of cling film.
Carefully slide the shaped roti onto the warm tawa.
Cook on medium-low heat for 3–4 minutes.
Cook the second side for another 3–4 minutes until golden.
Transfer to a plate and apply another generous piece of white butter or a spoon of ghee on top.

variants.name: Malai Boti
instructions: Cut your chicken breast into even 3/4-1 inch pieces - I got roughly 22 pieces from my 2 medium sized chicken breasts.
Mix the marinade ingredients with the chicken cubes and set aside to rest for a minimum of four hours and up to two days.
If using wooden skewers soak them in water for 30-minutes.
Air Fryer: 6 minutes per side at 390F.
Oven: Cover the exposed ends of wooden skewers with foil (to be safe) and bake on a greased tray lined with foil for 18-20 minutes at 375F, flipping halfway.
Grill: 6-8 minutes per side, but please bear in mind timings vary with grilling so keep a close eye on it!

alternate_methods.label: Alternate documented method
instructions: Cut into even 2-inch cubes. Evenly sized pieces are important on the grill: smaller pieces overcook before larger ones are done.

In a bartan (bowl), Mix malai (cream), cream cheese, dahi (yoghurt), adrak lahsun paste, kali mirch (black pepper), elaichi powder, and nimboo juice (lemon juice). Whisk everything together until smooth with no lumps — the cream cheese needs to be fully blended in.

Stir in the salted meat to the marinade and Mix by hand to massage it in, making sure every surface and every score cut is coated. Cover the bartan with cling film or transfer to a zip-lock bag. Refrigerate for at least 2 hours — 4-6 hours is.

If using a charcoal BBQ, light the coals 45 minutes before you plan to grill — Aim for them glowing white-hot with no visible flame. For a gas grill, preheat on high for 10-15 minutes. For an oven grill (broiler), preheat on the highest setting and position the.

Thread the marinated pieces onto metal seekhs (skewers) — about 5-6 pieces per skewer, leaving a small gap between each piece so heat can circulate. Put on the hot grill. Grill for 4-5 minutes without moving, until the underside develops golden-brown marks.
Chicken is done when the juices run completely clear when you press a piece — there should be no pink at all, especially in the score cuts.

instructions: Cut your beef fillet into wide strips - 2-3 inches wide. Put beef, onions, and salt in a heavy pot or a pressure cooker (follow manufacturer directions), Stir in 2.5 cups hot water, mix well and cook covered till tender.
Stir in more water if the meat starts to stick. Once the meat is tender and then crank up the heat to dry up the water.

While the meat is cooking Mix all the spices and dry roast them in a frying pan on medium heat till fragrant. Use a small knife to slit the side of the chillies and a small spoon to fill the chillies, reserve the leftover spice mix for later.

Warm 1/4 cup oil in a frying pan and cook the chillies stirring occasionally till they get tender and blistery. Remove the chillies with a slotted spoon, pour the hot oil over the pasandas and Stir in in half of what's left of your spice mix.
Cook on medium high heat for 5 minutes. Taste and adjust seasoning with more spice mix if needed. Stir in the stuffed chillies and gently mix them in. Cook on low heat for 5 minutes.
If you have extra spice mix leftover you can save it to stuff chilies another time or use it for cooking any curry.

ingredients.text: 1 cup gehun ka atta (whole wheat flour)
1/2 teaspoon lal mirch powder (red chilli powder)

instructions: In a large mixing bowl (paraat or any wide bowl), Mix the besan and atta. Stir in the ajwain, red chilli powder, and salt. Give it a quick mix with your fingers so everything is evenly distributed.
Stir in the finely chopped onion, green chilli, and fresh coriander to the flour mixture.
Stir in warm water a little at a time — start with 1/2 cup — and bring the dough together. Knead for 4–5 minutes until you have a smooth, firm dough. If it's sticky, Stir in a little dry atta.
Cover the dough with a damp cloth or an upturned bowl and let it rest for 15–20 minutes at room temperature.
Put your tawa (flat griddle pan) on the stove over medium heat. Let it heat for 2–3 minutes.

Divide the dough into 6 equal balls (about the size of a golf ball). Take one ball, flatten it slightly between your palms, and then use your belan (rolling pin) to roll it into a circle about 6–7 inches in diameter.
Carefully lift the rolled roti and Put it on the hot tawa. Cook on medium heat for about 90 seconds.
Using a chimta (tongs) or a flat spatula, carefully slide it under the roti and flip it.

Transfer the roti to a plate and immediately apply a generous knob of ghee while it's hot. That's the ajwain blooming in the heat, the onion caramelising at the edges, and the ghee doing what ghee does best.

variants.name: Mitho Lolo — Sindhi Sweet Jaggery Bread

ingredients.text: 2 cups gehun ka atta (whole wheat flour)
3-4 tablespoons ghee ya tail (extra ghee for cooking)

instructions: Pour the warm water over it and stir until the jaggery is completely dissolved. This may take 2–3 minutes of stirring. The liquid will be golden-brown, like a dark caramel.

In a large bowl, Mix the atta and saunf. Stir in the ghee (3 tablespoons) and rub it into the flour with your fingertips until the flour resembles breadcrumbs. and then pour in the dissolved jaggery water gradually, mixing and kneading as you go.
Cover the dough with a damp cloth and let it rest for 15–20 minutes. This relaxes the gluten and makes the dough easier to roll.
Put your tawa (flat griddle pan) on the stove over medium-low heat. This bread must be cooked on LOWER heat than a regular roti because the jaggery will burn quickly if the heat is too high.
Divide the dough into 6 portions. On a lightly floured chakla (rolling board), roll each portion into a circle about 5–6 inches in diameter and 5–6mm thick — notably thicker than a regular chapati.
Put the rolled lolo on the warm tawa. Stir in a teaspoon of ghee around the edges. Cook on medium-low heat for 3–4 minutes.
Stir in another teaspoon of ghee to the tawa. Cook the second side for another 3–4 minutes until it matches the first side in colour — deep golden-brown with slightly darker patches.
Transfer the lolo to a plate.

ingredients.text: 3/4-1 lb boneless chicken cut into big cubes (about 50% more for bone in)
1/2 teaspoon grated ginger or ginger paste
Heaped tbsp of Kasuri Methi (dried fenugreek - optional)

instructions: Warm a few tablespoons of oil in a pot and Stir in the diced onion, Cook on medium high heat till the edges start to take on a golden brown.
Optional: Stir in a diced green chilli (or two) for extra flavour.
Stir in the ginger and garlic and stir Cook for a minute.
Stir in the chicken and spices, saute on medium high heat until all the sides of the chicken pieces have changed colour.
Mix in the diced tomato, and 1/2-1 cup of hot water (more for stainless steel, less for non stick) and simmer for 20-25 minutes or until the chicken is tender.
Crank up the heat to dry up the excess water and Stir in your kasuri methi and saute for a minute.

Stir in your spinach - spinach is a naturally watery green so at this stage your goal is to cook the moisture out of the spinach and have the oil rise above your dish. This takes about 10-12 minutes on medium heat.
Adjust seasoning - a squeeze of lemon juice is lovely here, but you can also Stir in some garam masala, and/or extra chilies.

Stir in fried meat from before. Mix the meat into the onion’s masala, sautee for one minute. Stir in salt, red chili powder, turmeric, roasted cumin and coriander powder. Cook the masala on medium flame. Stir in a dash of water if needed.

When the meat is fully cooked Stir in the nuts paste for richness. Lastly Stir in the freshly crushed black pepper and fenugreek leaves (slightly crushing with the hands) and cream. Mix and let it simmer for another 5 – 10 minutes on low flame.
Warm one tablespoon of butter or ghee. As the butter melts Stir in garam masala powder, when it sizzles pour it on the mutton handi. Slight mix and let it cook on dam for 5 minutes.

variants.name: Lahori Mutton Karahi — Restaurant-Style Wok Curry

ingredients.text: 1 tsp Lal Mirch Powder (Red Chilli Powder)

instructions: Put a large, heavy karahi (wok) or wide heavy-bottomed pot on high heat. Stir in the tel (oil) and let it heat until shimmering — you can test by dropping a tiny piece of ginger in.
Stir in the mutton pieces to the hot oil. Do not stir for 2 minutes — let the meat develop a proper sear on one side.

Stir in the quartered tamatar (tomatoes), slit hari mirch (green chillies), lal mirch powder (red chilli powder), kali mirch (black pepper), and namak (salt). Stir everything together. The tomatoes will release a lot of liquid — keep the heat high.

This is the most important step. Once the tomatoes have broken down, continue cooking on high heat, stirring more frequently, until the masala thickens and the oil separates to the sides of the karahi — you'll see a pool of red-orange oil collecting around the edges. This process.

Once the masala is properly bhuno'd and oil-separated, Stir in 1⁄2 cup of hot water, stir, reduce heat to medium-low, and cover the karahi with a lid. Cook for 20-25 minutes until the mutton is tender — press a piece with a spoon.

Once the mutton is tender, increase heat back to high and bhuno (roast) the karahi again for 3-5 minutes, stirring constantly. Turn off the heat. Stir in malai (cream) and scatter julienned adrak (ginger strips) over the top.

A proper Lahori karahi is served in the karahi itself, placed directly on the table on a heat-proof stand. If you don't have a karahi, serve in a deep bowl but transfer immediately before the steam condenses and makes it watery.

instructions: In a bartan (bowl), Mix the lukewarm water, sugar, and yeast. Stir gently and leave undisturbed for 10 minutes.

Put your cast-iron tawa (flat griddle) or heaviest frying pan on the highest heat for at least 3–4 minutes.

Wet one side of the rolled naan lightly with water using your fingers. Cook for 2 minutes — you'll see bubbles forming on the top surface and the underside should have dark spots when you peek. Cook the second side for 1–1.5 minutes.

variants.name: Balochi Namkeen Gosht

ingredients.text: 3 tbsp charbi ya ghee (animal fat or ghee)

instructions: In a heavy-bottomed pot with a tight-fitting lid, arrange meat pieces. Stir in ghee, salt, kali mirch, tez patta, ginger slices, and quartered onion. DO NOT Stir in water.
Put pot on the lowest possible heat. Cook for 90-120 minutes without opening the lid. The meat will release its own juices and cook in them.
After 90 minutes, open carefully (the steam is very hot). If still firm, re-seal and cook another 20-30 minutes.
Once meat is tender, remove lid and increase heat to high for 5-8 minutes until the liquid reduces to almost nothing and meat is sizzling in its own fat.
Transfer to a simple platter. Light garnish of hara dhania only.

variants.name: Karachi Namkeen Gosht

ingredients.text: 2 inch piece adrak julienne (ginger for garnish)

instructions: Warm ghee in a heavy karahi or pot. Stir in zeera, let it pop. Stir in sliced ginger, whole garlic cloves, and sliced pyaaz.
Stir in mutton pieces, turn heat to high. Bhuno for 8-10 minutes, turning pieces to get colour on all sides.
SLOW COOK — THE KEY STEP: Stir in 1/2 cup water. Cover tightly and cook on medium-low heat for 70-80 minutes until meat is very tender.
In the last 10 minutes, uncover and cook on medium-high heat until all water has evaporated and the meat is sizzling in ghee.
Remove to a serving plate. The fresh garnish against the simple spiced meat is what makes namkeen gosht complete.

variants.name: KP Namkeen Karahi

ingredients.text: 5 tbsp ghee or tel (ghee or oil)
1.5 tsp sabut kali mirch (whole black peppercorns)

instructions: Put a steel karahi or heavy-bottomed wide pan over high heat and heat the ghee until it's very hot — almost smoking.
Stir in zeera seeds to the hot ghee — they'll sizzle and pop immediately. Stir in roughly smashed lehsan cloves and thickly sliced adrak. Stir 30 seconds.

Once meat is well-coloured, Stir in 1 cup hot water to the karahi. Reduce heat to medium-low, cover loosely, and cook for 50-60 minutes until mutton is very tender. Check every 15 minutes and Stir in small amounts of hot water if the liquid evaporates completely before the.

Once meat is tender, turn heat to the maximum. Stir in the chopped tamatar and slit hari mirch to the karahi. Bhuno everything on high heat for 8-10 minutes, stirring and pressing the tomatoes against the hot karahi to break them down rapidly.
Remove from heat. Stir in julienned ginger strips. Stir once to mix some of the garnish into the meat — the residual heat will wilt the coriander slightly, releasing its fragrance.

SERVE IN THE KARAHI — NEVER TRANSFER: Bring the karahi directly to the table on a wooden board or cloth. Do not transfer to another serving dish. Put additional fresh coriander, slit green chillies, and lemon wedges around the karahi for guests to Stir in themselves.

alternate_methods.label: Alternate documented method
instructions: NO BROWNING, JUST COOK: Put the mutton pieces directly into a dry karahi (wok). Stir in salt and black pepper.
Stir in half cup of water. Cover and cook on medium heat for 45-60 minutes, stirring every 15 minutes, until the meat is almost tender and most of the water has cooked off.
Once water is mostly gone, Stir in the ginger julienne and slit green chilies. Increase heat to high. bhuno (stir-Cook vigorously) — scraping the bottom of the karahi constantly for 10-15 minutes.
Stir in fresh coriander at the very end, give one last stir, and serve immediately from the karahi.
Transfer to a serving dish or serve straight from the karahi. The raw ginger garnish is the Namak Mandi marker — it adds a sharp, fresh contrast to the deep cooked flavors.

variants.name: Peshawari Namkeen Gosht
instructions: Stir in the pani (water), namak (salt), and HALF the crushed kali mirch (black pepper). Bring to a boil over high heat.
Once boiling, reduce the heat to low. Cover the pateela with a tight lid and let the gosht simmer gently for 1.5 to 2 hours. Check every 30 minutes to make sure there's still some pani in the pot.

Increase the heat to medium-high. Turn the pieces every 2-3 minutes using tongs or a chamcha (ladle) so all sides get exposure to the hot fat. Cook for about 10-15 minutes total until the edges are golden and crispy, with dark caramelised spots.
Toss the pieces gently to coat.

Transfer the gosht to a communal platter — a large thaal (round metal plate) is traditional. Pour ALL the remaining charbi (fat) from the pateela over the meat. Arrange raw pyaz (onion) rings, whole hari mirch (green chillies), and nimbu (lemon) wedges around the meat.

instructions: Make 3-4 diagonal slashes on each side of the trout. Mix salt, chili, ginger-garlic paste, and lemon juice. Marinate 20-30 minutes — no longer, acid will start cooking the flesh.
Warm ghee in a heavy pan large enough to fit the trout.
Lay the trout in the pan carefully. Do not move it for 4-5 minutes — let the skin set and crisp.
Cook the other side 4-5 minutes. Total time for a 350g trout is about 8-10 minutes — it should be cooked through without being dry.
Transfer to a plate.

variants.name: Nankhatai
instructions: Preheat your oven to 180°C (350°F). If you have a gas oven without a temperature gauge, medium heat is your target — most Pakistani ovens run slightly hot, so err on the lower side.

In a large mixing bowl, Stir in the semi-solid ghee and cheeni. Using a wooden spoon or your clean hand, beat them together vigorously for 3-4 minutes until the mixture becomes pale, fluffy, and somewhat light in texture.
In a separate bowl, Mix the maida, besan, suji, elaichi powder, and baking powder. Whisk them together with a fork for 30 seconds to distribute evenly.

Stir in the dry flour mixture to the creamed ghee-sugar in two additions, mixing gently with a spoon or your hand between each addition. The dough should come together into a soft, pliable ball that holds its shape when pressed — like Play-Doh.
Pinch off roughly equal portions of dough — about 1.5 tablespoons each, the size of a walnut. Roll each portion gently between your palms into a smooth ball.
Put the tray in the preheated oven on the middle rack. Bake for 15-18 minutes.

Remove from the oven and leave the nankhatai completely undisturbed on the tray for 15-20 minutes. After 15-20 minutes, they will have firmed up considerably. Gently transfer to a wire rack or plate to cool completely — another 20-30 minutes.

instructions: BROWN YOUR ONIONS — THIS IS NON-NEGOTIABLE: Heat ghee in a heavy-bottomed deg (pot) or pressure cooker over medium-high heat. Stir in sliced pyaaz and Cook, stirring frequently, for 12-15 minutes until they turn a deep mahogany brown. Not light golden — we're talking proper brown like strong.

Reduce heat to medium. Stir in adrak-lehsan paste and Cook for 2 minutes until the raw smell disappears — Continue until it smells nutty rather than sharp. Stir in nihari masala and lal mirch powder, stir everything together, and Stir in a splash of water to prevent burning.

Stir in the beef shank and nalli pieces to the pot. Increase heat to high and bhuno (stir-Cook) the meat with the masala for 5-7 minutes until every piece is coated and the meat has some colour on it.
Stir in 1.5 litres of hot water to the pot and bring to a vigorous boil. Once foam stops appearing (about 5 minutes), reduce heat to the lowest setting, cover tightly, and cook for 3 hours.

After 3 hours, the meat should be very tender — test by pressing a piece with a spoon. Mix aata with 4 tablespoons of water to make a smooth, lump-free paste. Fish out about a cup of hot gravy from the pot, whisk in the aata slurry, and.
In a small pan, heat 1 tablespoon of ghee until smoking hot, Stir in a pinch of red chilli powder and immediately pour this tarka over the nihari surface. Do not stir — let it sit on top.
Ladle nihari into deep bowls or a large serving dish.

variants.name: Bone Marrow Nihari

ingredients.text: 1 tsp lal mirch tarka (red chilli for tempering)

instructions: Put nalli pieces in a large pot, cover with cold water, Stir in 1 tsp salt, and bring to a hard boil. Boil for 5 minutes, and then drain completely and rinse bones under cold water. This blanching step removes impurities and blood from the bones — skipping.
In a heavy deg, heat ghee on medium-high. Stir in pyaaz and Cook for 18-20 minutes, stirring frequently, until they're a very deep mahogany.
To the fried onions, Stir in adrak-lehsan paste, crushed badi elaichi, nihari masala, kali mirch, and a splash of water. Bhuno for 5 minutes. Stir in blanched nalli and gosht.
LONG SLOW COOK — 4 TO 5 HOURS: Stir in 2 litres of hot water, bring to a boil, skim foam, and then reduce to the lowest possible heat. Cover tightly. Cook for 4-5 hours minimum.
After 4+ hours, the marrow should be loose in the bones. Stir it in thoroughly.
Mix aata with water into a smooth slurry. Stir in to a cup of hot nihari gravy, whisk smooth, pour back into pot. Simmer 25-30 minutes until gravy is thick enough to coat a spoon generously.
This nihari deserves a grand presentation. Cover the surface with julienned ginger strips, a mountain of fresh hara dhania, slit hari mirch, and lemon wedges around the edges.

And then Stir in your Nihari Masala Mix and 7 cups of water and stir well. Pressure cook for 45-50 minutes or slow cook for 4-5 hours undisturbed to get beautifully tender meat. For slow cooking stove top, bring the mixture to a boil and then let it simmer covered.
Crush the onions and mix in, bring the nihari to a boil. When ready to eat and then dissolve 1/3 cup atta in 1 cup water and whisk briskly as you Stir in it to the nihari.
The nihari will thicken as it cooks - 10 to 15 minutes. Adjust consistency per liking (more water or atta+water), just remember you need to simmer after adding it to lose the raw taste.

variants.name: Classic Lahori Nihari

ingredients.text: 1 tbsp Lal Mirch Powder (Red Chilli Powder)

instructions: Put 2 tbsp gandum ka atta (wheat flour) in a small, dry pan — no oil, no ghee. Put on medium-low heat and stir constantly with a chamcha (spoon). The atta will slowly change colour from white to pale gold to a toasty brown — this takes about.
Warm the desi ghee in a heavy-bottomed degh (large pot) or Dutch oven on medium heat. Stir in the sliced pyaz (onions). Stir every minute or so for about 15-20 minutes.

Stir in adrak lehsan paste (ginger-garlic paste) to the remaining pyaz in the degh. Stir for 2 minutes until the raw smell disappears — you'll know because the sharp, nose-prickling garlic smell turns into something warm and fragrant. Don't let it burn — if it starts sticking, Stir.
Stir in the beef nalli (shank pieces) and extra nalli (marrow bones) to the degh. Turn the heat to high. Using a large chamcha (ladle), turn the meat to brown all sides — about 5-7 minutes total.

Sprinkle in the nihari masala, lal mirch powder (red chilli powder), haldi (turmeric), and namak (salt). Stir everything well to coat every piece of meat — the spices should sizzle and become fragrant within 30 seconds.

Stir in the hot pani (water) — pour it in slowly to avoid a steam explosion. Bring to a boil on high heat (this takes about 5 minutes). Once boiling, reduce to the absolute lowest flame your stove can manage.

After the long cook, the marrow should have mostly melted into the gravy. If there are still marrow bones with intact marrow, use a spoon to scoop the soft, fatty marrow out of the bones and stir it into the gravy. If it's still resisting, cook for another.

Take the roasted atta you prepared in Step 1 and mix it with about 4 tbsp warm water in a small bowl to make a smooth slurry — no lumps. Slowly stir this into the nihari, a little at a time. Cook on low heat for another 30.
Ladle the nihari into deep bowls — a generous amount of the dark, glistening gravy with chunks of gosht and any remaining bone pieces.

3-4 tbsp sliced green onion - green parts (7-10g)

instructions: Mix all the sandwich ingredients you are using in a bowl and mix well. Aim for a homogenous almost paste like mix.
Divide your mixture amongst 8 of the cut squares and spread.

ingredients.item: melted butter plus extra for basting
ingredients.text: 1 tbsp melted butter plus extra for basting

instructions: Mix all the kabab ingredients in a bowl, mix just enough to Mix.
Set aside for 30 minutes to a few hours (if waiting a few hours and then please refrigerate).
Half an hour before you are ready to cook and then take the mix out of the fridge to bring to room temperature.
Warm a non stick frying pan or grill pan with a little oil.
Shape kababs with lightly oiled hands and gently Put in the pan.
Cook 2-3 minutes on each side on medium high heat for a lovely sear.

variants.name: Pakistani Chinese Beef Chilli Dry
instructions: Pour a lug of oil into a hot wok and stir Cook the garlic till it starts to sizzle and change coloue.

Stir in the strips of green pepper and chillies as well as the remaining ingredients, stir Cook on high for 2-3 minutes, taste, adjust seasoning if needed with vinegar, pepper and soy. (I always Stir in more!).

variants.name: Pakistani Dum Aloo

ingredients.item: yellow or red potatoes peeled and diced ((approx 4-cm)⁣)
ingredients.text: 750 g yellow or red potatoes peeled and diced ((approx 4-cm)⁣)
1/4 cup vegetable or olive oil (I use @maisonorphee ⁣)

ingredients.item: red onion (sliced thinly into half-moon shapes (approx 1 cup yield)⁣)
ingredients.text: 1 small red onion (sliced thinly into half-moon shapes (approx 1 cup yield)⁣)

ingredients.preparation: coarsely chopped, including its sweet stems⁣
ingredients.text: Fresh coriander (coarsely chopped, including its sweet stems⁣)

instructions: Put a large pot (which has a lid) on medium-high heat and Stir in oil.
When shimmering, Stir in onions. sauté the onions continuously for 10-15 minutes. They should be wilted and golden brown along the edges.
When onions are golden brown, Stir in garlic and ginger and continue to sauté for 2-3 minutes.
Stir in turmeric, ground coriander, ground cumin, and chili flakes. Mix to Mix, and then Stir in tomato sauce. Stir/sauté (bhuno) for 3-5 minutes.
Stir in potatoes, green chilies, 1 tsp salt, and 1 cup of water, and then turn heat to low and cover with a lid.
Allow to cook till potatoes are fork tender. Depending on the type of potatoes you are using, this should take 15-20 minutes.
Mix into the gravy.
Stir in second cup of water and allow to gently simmer, without lid.
Before serving, Stir in fresh cilantro, and enjoy with lemon wedges.

variants.name: Beef Keema Lasagna
variants.culinary_context: A Pakistani home-style adaptation of an Italian-inspired pasta dish, using ingredients and flavours common in Pakistan.
instructions: Heat the oil and cook the onions until golden at the edges. Add garlic and beef mince, breaking it up until fully browned and no pink remains.
Stir in cumin, chilli and oregano. Add tomatoes, tomato paste, half the salt and pepper; simmer for 20 minutes until thick but still spoonable.
Make a white sauce by cooking butter and flour for 90 seconds, then whisking in warm milk. Simmer until lightly thick and season.
Heat the oven to 190°C and prepare the sheets according to the packet if they are not oven-ready.
Layer keema sauce, lasagna sheets, white sauce and cheeses, finishing with white sauce and cheese.
Bake covered for 25 minutes and uncovered for 20 minutes. Rest for 15 minutes so the layers set before slicing.

variants.name: Chicken Lasagna
variants.culinary_context: A Pakistani home-style adaptation of an Italian-inspired pasta dish, using ingredients and flavours common in Pakistan.
instructions: Heat the oil and soften the onion. Add garlic and chicken mince; break it up and cook until no pink remains.
Add tomatoes, tomato paste, oregano, chilli flakes, half the salt and pepper. Simmer uncovered for 18–20 minutes until thick.
For the white sauce, melt butter, whisk in flour for 90 seconds, then gradually whisk in warm milk. Simmer until it coats a spoon and season.
Heat the oven to 190°C. If the lasagna sheets require pre-cooking, prepare them according to the packet.
Layer meat sauce, sheets, white sauce and cheeses in a baking dish, repeating and ending with white sauce and cheese.
Cover and bake for 25 minutes, uncover and bake for 15–20 minutes until browned. Rest for 15 minutes before cutting.

variants.name: Vegetable Lasagna
variants.culinary_context: A Pakistani home-style adaptation of an Italian-inspired pasta dish, using ingredients and flavours common in Pakistan.
instructions: Heat the oil and soften the onion. Add mushrooms and cook until their liquid evaporates, then add courgettes and peppers for 5 minutes.
Stir in garlic, tomatoes, tomato paste, oregano, salt and pepper. Simmer uncovered for 15 minutes, then fold in spinach until wilted.
Heat the oven to 190°C and prepare the lasagna sheets according to the packet if necessary.
Spread a little vegetable sauce in the dish. Layer sheets, vegetable sauce, spoonfuls of cottage cheese and grated cheeses.
Repeat the layers and finish with sauce and grated cheese. Cover and bake for 25 minutes.
Uncover and bake for 15–20 minutes until golden. Rest for 15 minutes before cutting.

variants.name: Creamy Chicken Fajita Pasta
variants.culinary_context: A Pakistani home-style adaptation of an Italian-inspired pasta dish, using ingredients and flavours common in Pakistan.
instructions: Cook the penne until al dente. Reserve 1 cup pasta water and drain.
Combine paprika, cumin, chilli, oregano and salt. Coat the chicken with half the spice mix.
Heat 1 tablespoon oil and cook the chicken for 6–8 minutes until browned and 74°C inside. Remove it from the pan.
Add the remaining oil and stir-fry the onion and peppers over high heat for 4 minutes so they retain some bite. Add garlic and the remaining spice mix for 30 seconds.
Reduce the heat. Add milk and cream, simmer gently for 4 minutes, then melt in the cheese without boiling hard.
Return the chicken, add the pasta and toss until coated. Loosen with pasta water and finish with citrus juice.

variants.name: Chicken Tikka Pasta
variants.culinary_context: A Pakistani home-style adaptation of an Italian-inspired pasta dish, using ingredients and flavours common in Pakistan.

ingredients.text: 600 g boneless chicken (cut into 2 cm pieces)

instructions: Mix the chicken with yogurt, tikka masala, lemon juice and half the salt. Marinate for at least 20 minutes while preparing the other ingredients.
Boil the fusilli until al dente, reserving 1 cup of pasta water before draining.
Heat the oil in a wide pan. Cook the marinated chicken in a single layer for 8–10 minutes until lightly charred at the edges and 74°C inside. Remove from the pan.
In the same pan, cook the onion and peppers for 4 minutes. Add garlic, then tomato puree and simmer for 8 minutes.
Lower the heat, stir in the cream and return the chicken. Add the pasta and enough reserved water to make a silky sauce.
Taste for salt, finish with fresh coriander and serve hot.

variants.name: Chicken White Sauce Pasta
variants.culinary_context: A Pakistani home-style adaptation of an Italian-inspired pasta dish, using ingredients and flavours common in Pakistan.

ingredients.text: 500 g boneless chicken breast (cut into bite-size pieces)

instructions: Boil the pasta in well-salted water until just al dente. Reserve 1 cup of pasta water, then drain.
Heat the oil in a wide pan. Season the chicken with half the salt and pepper, then cook for 6–8 minutes until browned and the centre reaches 74°C. Transfer to a plate.
In the same pan, cook the bell pepper and sweetcorn for 3 minutes. Add the garlic for the final 30 seconds, then transfer the vegetables to the chicken.
Melt the butter over medium-low heat. Whisk in the flour and cook for 90 seconds without browning. Add the warm milk gradually, whisking until smooth.
Simmer the sauce for 4–5 minutes until it coats a spoon. Stir in the cheese, oregano, chilli flakes and remaining seasoning.
Fold in the pasta, chicken and vegetables. Loosen with a little reserved pasta water and serve while creamy.

variants.name: Creamy Chicken Alfredo Pasta
variants.culinary_context: A Pakistani home-style adaptation of an Italian-inspired pasta dish, using ingredients and flavours common in Pakistan.
instructions: Boil the fettuccine in salted water until al dente. Reserve 1 cup of cooking water before draining.
Season the chicken with salt and pepper. Heat the oil with 1 tablespoon butter and cook the chicken for 6–8 minutes, turning until browned and 74°C at the thickest point. Set aside.
Lower the heat and melt the remaining butter in the same pan. Cook the garlic for 30 seconds without colouring it.
Add the cream and milk. Bring only to a gentle simmer, then stir in the parmesan a handful at a time until smooth.
Add the drained pasta and chicken. Toss over low heat, adding reserved pasta water little by little until the sauce is glossy rather than thick or clumpy.
Taste for seasoning, scatter over parsley and serve immediately.

variants.name: Creamy Chicken and Mushroom Pasta
variants.culinary_context: A Pakistani home-style adaptation of an Italian-inspired pasta dish, using ingredients and flavours common in Pakistan.
instructions: Boil the pasta until al dente. Save 1 cup of its cooking water, then drain.
Season the chicken. Heat the oil and 1 tablespoon butter, then cook the chicken until golden and 74°C inside. Transfer to a plate.
Add the remaining butter and mushrooms. Cook over medium-high heat for 6–7 minutes until their released liquid evaporates and the edges brown.
Add garlic and thyme for 30 seconds. Pour in milk and cream, then simmer gently for 4 minutes.
Stir in parmesan, return the chicken and add the pasta. Toss with enough reserved water to keep the sauce fluid.
Finish with black pepper, check the salt and serve immediately.

variants.name: Spicy Chicken Red Sauce Pasta
variants.culinary_context: A Pakistani home-style adaptation of an Italian-inspired pasta dish, using ingredients and flavours common in Pakistan.
instructions: Cook the penne in salted water until one minute short of al dente. Reserve 1 cup cooking water and drain.
Heat 1 tablespoon oil. Season and sauté the chicken for 6–8 minutes until browned and cooked to 74°C, then remove.
Add the remaining oil and soften the onion and bell pepper for 5 minutes. Stir in garlic, chilli flakes, chilli powder and oregano for 30 seconds.
Add tomato paste, crushed tomatoes, sugar and salt. Simmer uncovered for 12–15 minutes until the raw tomato taste has gone.
Return the chicken and add the pasta. Toss for 2 minutes, loosening with reserved water so the sauce clings evenly.
Adjust chilli and seasoning before serving.

variants.name: Vegetable Red Sauce Pasta
variants.culinary_context: A Pakistani home-style adaptation of an Italian-inspired pasta dish, using ingredients and flavours common in Pakistan.
instructions: Cook the pasta in salted water until al dente. Reserve 1 cup cooking water and drain.
Heat the oil and soften the onion and carrot for 5 minutes. Add the peppers, courgette and mushrooms and cook for another 6 minutes.
Stir in garlic, oregano and chilli flakes for 30 seconds, followed by the tomato paste.
Add crushed tomatoes, sugar and salt. Simmer uncovered for 12–15 minutes until slightly reduced and the vegetables are tender.
Add the pasta and toss for 2 minutes, using reserved water as needed so the sauce coats every piece.
Taste for seasoning and serve hot.

variants.name: Spaghetti with Beef Meat Sauce
variants.culinary_context: A Pakistani home-style adaptation of an Italian-inspired pasta dish, using ingredients and flavours common in Pakistan.
instructions: Heat the oil and cook the onion and carrot over medium heat for 6–7 minutes until soft. Add garlic for 30 seconds.
Add the beef mince, breaking it into small pieces. Cook until well browned with no pink remaining.
Stir in tomato paste, oregano, thyme and chilli. Add crushed tomatoes, sugar, salt and pepper.
Simmer partially covered for 25 minutes, stirring occasionally, until thick and rich. Add a splash of water if it catches.
Meanwhile boil the spaghetti until al dente, reserving 1 cup of its water before draining.
Toss the spaghetti with enough meat sauce to coat, loosening with pasta water. Spoon the remaining sauce over each serving.

variants.name: Pakistani Homestyle Chicken Jalfrezi (Boneless Chicken)

ingredients.text: 1/2 large onion, diced, approx half cup

instructions: Warm 3-4 tbsp of oil in a wok or saucepan with a lid.
Stir in the onions and saute on medium heat until the edges start to change colour.
Stir in the chicken, ginger paste, garlic paste, and spices and saute until the colour changes.
Mix in the tomatoes and simmer covered until the chicken is tender. This takes me roughly 20 minutes from previously frozen chicken, fresh is usually quicker.

Stir in the soy sauce, green peppers, black pepper, and one green chili and mix well and cook partially covered until the green pepper is cooked to your desired doneness. Tender-crisp takes 5 to 7 minutes.
Final steps: adjust consistency, and then seasoning, and Stir in the remaining green chilies slit lengthwise.

variants.name: Cheesy Baked Macaroni
variants.culinary_context: A Pakistani home-style adaptation of an Italian-inspired pasta dish, using ingredients and flavours common in Pakistan.
instructions: Heat the oven to 190°C. Boil the macaroni for 2 minutes less than the packet recommends, then drain.
Melt 3 tablespoons butter. Whisk in flour and cook for 90 seconds. Gradually whisk in warm milk and simmer until lightly thickened.
Remove from the heat. Stir in mustard, pepper, half the cheddar and half the mozzarella until smooth, then season to taste.
Combine the sauce with the macaroni and transfer to a greased baking dish.
Mix the breadcrumbs with the remaining melted butter. Scatter the remaining cheeses and buttered crumbs over the macaroni.
Bake for 20–25 minutes until bubbling and golden. Rest for 8 minutes before serving.

variants.name: Creamy Chicken Macaroni Salad
variants.culinary_context: A Pakistani home-style adaptation of an Italian-inspired pasta dish, using ingredients and flavours common in Pakistan.
instructions: Poach or pan-cook the chicken until it reaches 74°C. Cool completely, then cut into small cubes.
Boil the macaroni until just tender. Drain, rinse under cold water and leave until completely cool and dry.
Blanch the peas for 2 minutes and cool them. Place the macaroni, chicken, peas, corn, carrot and pepper in a large bowl.
Whisk mayonnaise, yogurt, mustard, lemon juice, sugar, pepper and salt until smooth.
Fold the dressing through the salad. Chill, covered, for at least 1 hour.
Stir before serving and keep refrigerated; do not leave the salad at room temperature for more than 2 hours.

variants.name: Pakistani Keema Macaroni
variants.culinary_context: A Pakistani home-style adaptation of an Italian-inspired pasta dish, using ingredients and flavours common in Pakistan.
instructions: Boil the macaroni until just al dente, drain and set aside.
Heat the oil and cook the onions until light golden. Add ginger-garlic paste and stir for 1 minute.
Add the beef mince. Break it up thoroughly and cook over medium-high heat until no pink remains and its moisture has evaporated.
Add chilli, cumin, coriander, salt, tomatoes and tomato paste. Cook for 10–12 minutes, stirring, until the tomatoes collapse and oil begins to separate.
Add the pepper and peas with 0.5 cup water. Cover and cook for 5 minutes, then stir in garam masala.
Fold in the macaroni and cook together for 3 minutes. Finish with coriander and adjust seasoning.

variants.name: Pakistani Chicken Macaroni
variants.culinary_context: A Pakistani home-style adaptation of an Italian-inspired pasta dish, using ingredients and flavours common in Pakistan.
instructions: Boil the macaroni until al dente, rinse briefly with cool water and drain well.
Heat 1 tablespoon oil in a wok or wide pan. Season and stir-fry the chicken for 6–8 minutes until browned and 74°C inside, then remove.
Add the remaining oil and stir-fry onion, carrots and cabbage over high heat for 3 minutes. Add peppers and garlic for another 2 minutes.
Mix ketchup, chilli garlic sauce, soy sauce, vinegar and black pepper. Pour the mixture into the pan and let it bubble for 30 seconds.
Return the chicken and add the macaroni. Toss over high heat for 2–3 minutes until evenly coated and hot.
Taste before adding more salt because soy sauce is already salty.

variants.name: Pakistani Vegetable Macaroni
variants.culinary_context: A Pakistani home-style adaptation of an Italian-inspired pasta dish, using ingredients and flavours common in Pakistan.
instructions: Boil the macaroni until al dente, rinse briefly and drain thoroughly.
Heat the oil in a wok. Stir-fry onion and carrots over high heat for 2 minutes.
Add cabbage, peppers, peas, corn and garlic. Continue stir-frying for 4–5 minutes so the vegetables cook but retain some bite.
Mix ketchup, chilli garlic sauce, soy sauce, vinegar, pepper and salt, then add to the wok.
Fold in the macaroni and toss over high heat for 2–3 minutes until evenly coated and steaming.
Taste and balance with a little extra vinegar or chilli sauce if needed.

variants.name: Pakistani Masala Omelette

ingredients.item: ghee (or 1 tbsp neutral oil (sunflower or corn))
ingredients.text: 1 tbsp ghee (or 1 tbsp neutral oil (sunflower or corn))

instructions: Pre-heat your grill/broiler.
Beat two eggs in a small bowl and Stir in onion, coriander, green chili, haldi, cayenne and salt. Whisk well.
Put a small frying pan on medium heat and Stir in ghee/oil.
Pour egg mixture into frying pan and keep swirling till the egg mixture is well distributed.
After 2-3 minutes, you will see the edges begin to crisp up. At this point, you can either flip the omelette over, or if Aim for to be cautious, Put it under the grill till golden, about 2 minutes.

variants.dish_family: Pakistani Palak Paneer - Richly flavored, Dhaba Style

ingredients.preparation: recommended: south asian, more in post
ingredients.text: 340 g frozen spinach (recommended: south asian, more in post)
1 tbsp crushed garlic or garlic paste
1/2 tbsp grated ginger or ginger paste

instructions: If you are using prefried paneer or don't want fried paneer you can skip this step, but otherwise cut your paneer into small cubes and pan Cook in a little oil until golden on each side. Soak the paneer briefly in salted water and drain - this will. Warm 3-4 tbsp of oil in a saute pan or wok on medium high.

Stir in your diced onions, green chilies, and cumin seeds to the pan and cook till the onions take on an amber hue. Stir in in your ginger and garlic, give it a stir and cook for a minute to cook the rawness out.
Stir in in your tomatoes, salt, chili flakes, and turmeric. Cover your saute pan with a lid and cook for 2 minutes.

Continue to cook the tomato mixture for another 3-5 minutes or until the oil starts to rise above the tomato mix. You can put your frozen spinach in, turn the heat down to medium, and cook covered for 5 minutes.

Remove the lid, mix well, and cook uncovered on medium high heat for another 5-7 minutes, the mix will look cohesive and rich. Run your mix (and 2 ice cubes if you are in a rush) through a chopper, mini food processor or blender along with 1-2 tbsp of cream (or yoghurt).

Put your mix back in the pan along with 1 tbsp more of oil and your kasuri methi. the extra oil is because your blended mix will burn quickly otherwise. Cook on low heat, covered for about 5-7 minutes or until the mix starts to separate a little.
Stir in your paneer cubes, cook for low, covered for 5 minutes and serve!

Warm or mix the vinegar, salt, sugar and measured spices until the salt and sugar dissolve.
Pack the vegetables into a clean jar and cover completely with the pickling liquid.

ingredients.text: 1 tsp saffron strands, (crushed in a pestle and mortar)

Beat the cream in a chilled bowl with a whisk or an electric mixer just until it holds a loose peak.
Put milk in a medium-sized sauce pan on medium-low heat. Stir in cardamom seeds and bring to a simmer.
While milk is still warm (it should not be hot), Stir in saffron water, honey and cardamom powder. Stir well to incorporate.
Transfer to serving glasses and Stir in dollop of cream and sprinkle with crushed pistachios before serving.

In go the potatoes and salt, give it all a little whirl and let the potatoes cook for 20 minutes on low heat. Do not Stir in water.
When the potatoes are done taste, adjust seasoning and and then Stir in the chopped dill. Gently stir and cover the pot.

variants.name: Pakistani Style Deep-fried Shrimp Recipe

ingredients.text: 1 pound ~500 grams jumbo shrimp or prawn (peeled, deveined and thawed)
1 cup neutral oil (canola, sunflower or vegetable )

instructions: In a large bowl, Stir in the beaten egg and all marinade ingredients (cilantro, chili, ginger, garlic, salt, red chili powder and lemon juice). Mix until well-blended.
Stir in shrimp/prawn to the marinade, and coat well.
Stir in 1 cup flour, baking soda, white pepper and salt. Mix well. Stir in water gradually, mixing it with a fork until well-blended.
Drain the egg marinade into the batter mixture, leaving the shrimp/prawn behind.
Beat the egg marinade into the flour batter with a fork until smooth.
In a separate plate or bowl, pour 1⁄2 all purpose flour to coat the shrimp/prawn, and Put it right besides the stove. In a small saucepan, heat oil.
Dip the shrimp/prawn into the batter, and and then coat it really well with the dry flour. Spoon the flour over it if you have to, and Stir in more as needed.

Once the oil is hot, gradually lower the battered shrimp into saucepan, and Cook each side for roughly 1 1⁄2 minute until crispy. Once the oil is piping hot, you can gradually lower the heat as you make your way to the rest of the shrimp/prawn.
Once done, Put the prepared shrimp/prawn on it to drain.

variants.name: Pakistani Tomato Omelette

ingredients.item: chopped fresh coriander/cilantro leaves and stems
ingredients.text: 2 tbsp chopped fresh coriander/cilantro leaves and stems (1 tbsp + 1 tbsp)

instructions: Put a saucepan on medium-high heat and Stir in oil.

After the oil has heated up for two minutes, Stir in the garlic, haldi and zeera powder. Sauté till the garlic is golden around the edges (make sure it does not turn brown, as it will taste bitter and rancid).

Stir in chopped tomatoes, chili flakes and salt and stir (careful, tomatoes may splatter). Cover the saucepan with a lid and turn heat to medium. Leave to simmer for twenty minutes till tomato sauce has thickened.
Remove from heat and set aside.
Whisk eggs and set aside.

Put frying pan on medium-high heat and Stir in oil, onions, salt, dhania powder, haldi and sauté till onions are golden and caramelised around the edges. This requires constant stirring and will take about 10-15 minutes.
When onions are caramelised (bronze), Stir in red chili flakes and pour the whisked eggs in. Gently stir, mixing onions with the whisked eggs. Turn heat down to medium.

Working quickly (because you don't want the egg mixture to overcook), Stir in tomato sauce into the egg mixture a teaspoon at a time, creating a dotted pattern across the omelette. Allow egg mixture to cook for 3-4 more minutes, keeping a keen eye on the pan. As.
For a soft-centred omelette, keep it under the grill for 3 minutes.

variants.name: Chocolate Trifle
variants.culinary_context: A familiar international-style dessert commonly prepared in Pakistani homes, bakeries or celebrations.

ingredients.text: 400 ml whipping cream (whipped to soft peaks)

instructions: Mix custard powder with 150 ml milk. Heat the remaining milk and sugar, whisk in the slurry and cook until thick.
Remove from the heat and stir in 100 g chopped chocolate until smooth. Cover the surface and cool completely.
Layer half the cake in a serving bowl, followed by half the chocolate custard and half the biscuit crumbs.
Repeat the cake, custard and biscuit layers.
Top with whipped cream and the remaining 50 g chopped chocolate.
Cover and chill for at least 4 hours before serving.

variants.name: Mango Trifle
variants.culinary_context: A familiar international-style dessert commonly prepared in Pakistani homes, bakeries or celebrations.

ingredients.text: 400 g plain sponge cake (cut into cubes)
300 ml whipping cream (whipped to soft peaks)

instructions: Mix the custard powder with 100 ml milk. Heat the remaining milk and sugar, whisk in the slurry and cook until thick. Cover the surface and cool fully.
Set aside one-quarter of the best mango pieces for the top.
Arrange half the sponge in a bowl and drizzle with half the mango juice. Add half the mango and half the cooled custard.
Repeat the sponge, juice, mango and custard layers.
Spread whipped cream over the top and decorate with reserved mango and pistachios.
Cover and chill for at least 4 hours. Keep refrigerated until serving.

variants.name: Pakistani Fruit Custard Trifle
variants.culinary_context: A familiar international-style dessert commonly prepared in Pakistani homes, bakeries or celebrations.

ingredients.text: 400 g plain sponge cake (cut into cubes)

ingredients.item: halal-certified jelly crystals or agar jelly
ingredients.text: 85 g halal-certified jelly crystals or agar jelly (prepared and set)
400 ml whipping cream (whipped to soft peaks)

instructions: Prepare the halal-certified or agar-based jelly according to its packet, chill until firmly set, then cut into cubes.
Mix custard powder with 150 ml of the milk until smooth. Heat the remaining milk with sugar, whisk in the slurry and cook until thick. Cover the surface and cool completely.
Place half the sponge in a deep serving bowl. Add half the drained fruit, apple, banana and jelly.

ingredients.text: 4-6 tbsp Makhan ya Ghee (Butter or Ghee)

instructions: In a large bartan (bowl), Mix the atta (flour), salt, and one tablespoon of oil or ghee. Gradually Stir in lukewarm water, mixing with your hand as you go. Knead the dough for 7-8 full minutes — it should be smooth, soft, and slightly tacky but not sticky.

Boil the potatoes whole and unpeeled in salted water until completely tender — a knife should slide in with zero resistance, 20-25 minutes. Drain, peel while still hot (use a cloth to hold them), and mash immediately.

Mix the cooled mashed aloo with hara dhania (coriander), hari mirch (green chillies), lal mirch, ajwain (carom seeds), zeera (cumin), nimbu (lemon) juice, and namak (salt) to taste. Mix thoroughly. Roll into balls approximately 40g each (about the size of a walnut).

Divide the rested dough into the same number of balls as filling portions. On a lightly floured surface, roll a dough ball into a circle about 15cm in diameter. roll this stuffed ball out again, slowly and gently, into a circle 20-22cm in diameter.

Warm a tawa (flat griddle) or heavy flat pan over medium-high heat until hot — a few drops of water flicked on it should evaporate within 2 seconds. Cook for 60-90 seconds — you'll see the surface start to look drier and small bubbles will form. Stir in.

The paratha is done when both sides have golden-brown patches and the bread has cooked through — no doughy-white patches should remain. Press the edges down firmly during cooking — the edges cook last and need direct contact with the tawa. Stir in a small knob of cold.
Aloo paratha is a serve-immediately dish — unlike naan which holds reasonably well, paratha loses its crisp-outside-soft-inside texture after 10 minutes.

ingredients.item: for garnish Hara Dhania aur Adrak
ingredients.text: for garnish Hara Dhania aur Adrak (Fresh Coriander and Ginger)

instructions: Put the paya (trotters) in a large degh (heavy-bottomed pot) with enough cold water to cover by 3 inches. Stir in the whole onion, ginger slices, a teaspoon of salt, and half the whole spices. Bring to a full, rolling boil over high heat.

SLOW BRAISE — THE LONG COOK: Return the cleaned paya to the degh with 2 litres of fresh cold water, the remaining whole spices, and half a teaspoon of salt. Bring to a boil, and then reduce heat to the lowest possible setting. Cover with the lid slightly.

About 30 minutes before the paya are done, heat ghee in a separate karahi (wok) over medium-high heat. Stir in the finely chopped pyaz (onion) and Cook for 12-15 minutes until deep golden-brown — deeper than you'd go for most dishes.

Use a chamcha (ladle) to transfer the cooked paya into the masala karahi along with 2-3 ladlefuls of the broth. Stir well to coat the trotters in the spiced masala. Cook together for 10 minutes, stirring occasionally — the masala should be absorbed by the trotters.

Let everything simmer together on low heat for 20-25 minutes, partially covered. The broth should thicken slightly — it won't be as thick as a regular curry, but it should coat the back of a spoon. The finished paya should look like a deep brown, glossy gravy with.

Garnish generously with fresh julienned adrak (ginger) — not chopped, julienned, which is traditional and important for the texture contrast. Stir in chopped hara dhania (coriander), sliced hari mirch (green chilli), and a squeeze of nimbu (lemon).

instructions: In a small katori (bowl), mix the lukewarm water, sugar, and yeast. Stir once and leave for 8–10 minutes until foamy and fragrant.

Oil a large bowl, Put the dough inside, cover tightly with a damp cloth, and leave in a warm Put for 1–2 hours until doubled.
Set your oven to its absolute maximum — 250–260°C if possible. Heat it for at least 30 minutes.

Punch down the risen dough and divide into 4 large portions — remember, Peshawari Naan is big. Roll each portion into a smooth ball. On a lightly floured chakla (rolling board), use your hands and belan (rolling pin) to stretch and roll each ball into a large oval.

Using a flat board or a pizza peel dusted with flour, slide one naan onto the screaming hot pan in the oven. Bake for 3–5 minutes on the top rack. Watch through the oven glass — see the naan puff dramatically into large bubbles within the first 2.
The heat of the bread will melt the butter instantly and it will soak into all those little crags and bubbles.

instructions: Put the rice in a bowl and cover with cold water. Let it soak for 30 minutes minimum — the grains will absorb water and become soft enough to grind. Drain the water completely.
Stir in the zafran to this warm milk and let it sit for 10-15 minutes.

Pour the remaining milk into a heavy-bottomed pateela (saucepan) or degh. Put on medium heat and bring to a gentle boil, stirring frequently with a chamcha. Once it reaches a boil, reduce the heat to medium-low.

Stir in 2-3 tablespoons of the hot milk from the pot into your ground rice and mix it to form a smooth slurry — this prevents lumps when you Stir in it to the pot. pour this rice slurry slowly into the simmering milk while stirring constantly with.
Keep stirring continuously on medium-low heat for 20-25 minutes. It should coat the back of a spoon thickly.
Stir in the cheeni and stir until fully dissolved — about 2 minutes.
Fill each one about 3/4 full as the phirni won't expand but you need room for garnish. Let them cool at room temperature for 15-20 minutes, and then carefully transfer to the refrigerator.
Just before serving, arrange the sliced pista, badam, and gulab ki pattian on top of each phirni.

alternate_methods.label: Alternate documented method
instructions: Soak basmati rice for 30 minutes. Drain and Stir in to a blender with 1/4 cup of the milk. Blend to a coarse paste — not smooth powder, Aim for visible rice granules.
Pour remaining milk into a heavy-bottomed karahi. Bring to a boil over medium heat, stirring to prevent scorching. Reduce to medium-low.
Stir the rice paste once more (it settles) and then pour it into the hot milk in a thin stream while stirring constantly. Continue stirring on medium heat.
Cook, stirring frequently, for 15-20 minutes until the phirni is thick enough to coat a spoon — it should leave a clear trail when you draw a line through it on the back of a spoon.
Stir in sugar and stir to dissolve. Stir in saffron milk and cardamom powder. Cook for another 3-4 minutes.
Pour warm phirni into individual clay matke (pots). Let cool to room temperature for 30 minutes, and then refrigerate uncovered for at least 4 hours — overnight is perfect.

instructions: Cook half the sliced onions in 2 tbsp ghee in a heavy degh (pot) on medium-high heat, stirring frequently, until they turn deep golden-amber — 10-12 minutes. These will be used as garnish and they'll crisp up as they cool.

With the ghee still hot, Stir in the remaining sliced pyaz (onion) to the pot. Cook until translucent — just 4-5 minutes, not deep golden this time. Stir in the adrak lehsan paste (ginger-garlic paste) and stir for 2 minutes until the raw smell cooks off.

Stir in the boiled kabuli chana (chickpeas) to the pot and stir to coat them in the spiced ghee. Stir in the dahi (yoghurt) and stir until it's absorbed — about 1 minute. Stir in half the chopped hara dhaniya (coriander) and the slit hari mirch (green chillies).
Pour in the 3 cups of water or stock. The liquid should just cover the rice. Bring to a boil on high heat.

alternate_methods.label: Alternate documented method
instructions: Warm a heavy-bottom pot over medium-low heat. Stir in oil. Once it begins to shimmer, Stir in cloves, peppercorns, black cardamom and cumin seeds.

Remove lid, lower to a simmer on medium heat, and let the water boil out, about 7 to 8 minutes.
Once the water has boiled out, bring the heat down to the lowest possible point. Wrap tight fitting lid with a cotton cloth, cover pot with it, and let the rice steam for 8 to 10 minutes.
Remove from heat and Put on serving platter.

variants.name: Home-Style Chicken Pulao

1 tsp lal mirch powder (red chilli powder)

instructions: Warm ghee in a heavy pot. Stir in zeera and sabut garam masala — they'll sizzle and release fragrance within 30 seconds. Stir in sliced pyaz and cook on medium-high heat until deep golden, about 12-15 minutes.

variants.name: Kabuli Pulao (Afghan-Peshawari Rice)
instructions: Warm 2 tbsp ghee in a heavy degh (pot) on medium-high. Stir in the sliced pyaz (onion) and cook, stirring, for 12-15 minutes until deep golden-brown. Stir in the mutton/lamb pieces and sear on all sides until browned — about 5-7 minutes.

Remove the meat pieces from the stock and set aside — they'll be placed back on top of the finished rice. Strain the stock through a fine sieve into a measuring jug. You need exactly 3 cups of stock for 2 cups of rice — Stir in water.

Warm 2 tbsp ghee in a separate karai (wok) on medium heat. Stir in the julienned gaajar (carrots) and stir for 3-4 minutes until they begin to soften. Stir in the cheeni (sugar) and stir continuously — the sugar will melt, coat the carrots, and slowly caramelise.

In the same karai with remaining ghee, Cook the slivered badam (almonds) on medium heat for 60-90 seconds, stirring constantly, until pale golden. If using pista (pistachios), Stir in for the last 30 seconds.
Bring the 3 cups of strained stock to a boil in the cleaned degh. Stir in the soaked, drained basmati chawal (rice). Stir once, and then reduce heat to medium.

Once the stock is absorbed, reduce heat to the absolute lowest setting. Spread the caramelised carrots and kishmish (raisins) over the rice in a beautiful layer. Cover the degh tightly with foil first, and then the lid — the foil seals in the steam better than the lid.
Arrange the meat pieces on top.

variants.name: Kashmiri Sweet Pulao

Stir in water (550ml), the bloomed saffron milk, sugar, and salt. Stir once and bring to a boil. Reduce to lowest heat, cover tightly, and cook 18 minutes.
Open the pot and gently fluff the rice with a fork — it should be a glorious golden colour from the saffron. Transfer to a serving platter and scatter the toasted dry fruits all over the top.

Transfer to a wide, shallow serving platter. Arrange the toasted dry fruits — golden badam slices, plump kishmish, green pistachios, golden coconut flakes — generously and artfully across the golden saffron rice.

instructions: Wash your rice, soak it in cold water and set it aside.
Warm oil in a large pot (preferably non stick) and Stir in your whole spices - the cloves, black pepper, cardamom, and cinnamon. Cook for two minutes till fragrant.
In go the onions - these will take 6-10 minutes to caramelize. Aim for a dark brown colour - Stir in a splash of water immediately to stop the browning from turning into burning.
And then Stir in your ginger and garlic, stir Cook for two minutes till fragrant.
Stir in salt, coriander powder and red chilli powder. Cook for another 2 minutes.
And then Stir in the chicken and stir Cook it well till all of it turns white. The intent isn't to fully cook them, but to give the chicken a head start.
And then Stir in the rice, 3 1/4 cup water and 1 1/4 tsp salt. Stir to Mix and bring it to a boil.
Cover and simmer on medium heat for 10-15 minutes - essentially until the water is mostly absorbed.
Cook on low heat for another 10 minutes and then check for doneness.

variants.name: Wedding Pilau (Dawat Wala Pulao)

ingredients.text: 5 tbsp adrak lehsan paste (ginger garlic paste)

instructions: In the largest pot you have, Stir in mutton with 3 litres water, quartered onion, 2 tbsp adrak lehsan paste, yogurt (250g), half the whole spices, and generous salt. Bring to boil, and then simmer covered for 80-90 minutes until mutton is completely tender and falling off the.
Remove mutton. Strain the stock carefully. Simmer to reduce if needed or top up with water.
Warm all the ghee in the largest heavy pot. Stir in zeera, kali zeera, and remaining whole spices. Let them bloom for 1 minute — the fragrance should fill the room.
Stir in all the yakhni to the tarka pot. Bring to a rolling boil. Taste and adjust salt — season boldly.
Transfer to large serving platters — one won't be enough.
After the 15-minute rest, open the pot ceremonially — this is the moment guests have been waiting for. Transfer to the largest serving platter you have.

variants.name: Yakhni Pulao

ingredients.text: 1 set Kharay masalay barray (Large whole spices for yakhni)
1 set Kharay masalay chhotay (Small whole spices for frying)

instructions: In a large degh (pot), Stir in the gosht (meat), 1 whole pyaz (onion, halved), adrak (ginger), lehsan (garlic), and all the large kharay masalay (whole spices for yakhni). Stir in 5 cups of water and 1 teaspoon salt. Bring to a boil over high heat, skimming off.
Remove the cooked gosht pieces and set aside. Strain the broth through a fine sieve or muslin cloth, discarding all the boiled spices, onion, and aromatics. If you have more, reduce by boiling.
Warm ghee in a wide, heavy degh over medium-high heat. Stir in the 2 sliced onions. Cook for 15–18 minutes, stirring frequently, until deep golden brown — darker than you might think is right.

Stir in the small kharay masalay (green cardamom, cinnamon, cloves) to the onion-oil in the pot. Stir in the cooked gosht pieces back in. Cook the meat with the onions and spices for 3–4 minutes, turning occasionally, until the meat has picked up some colour.
Pour the measured yakhni (stock) into the pot. Bring to a full rolling boil over high heat. Stir in the drained soaked chawal (rice).

Once the yakhni has been mostly absorbed and the rice surface looks like a cratered moon (small steam holes forming), reduce heat to the absolute lowest setting. Cover the pot with a tight lid — seal the edges with a chapati dough rope or Put a damp cloth.
Turn off the heat. Leave the pot sealed for another 5 minutes off the heat — the residual steam finishes the rice.

alternate_methods.label: instant-pot
instructions: Mix all the yakhni ingredients along with 3.5 cups of water in your Instant Pot or pressure cooker. Stir and set on Manual for 15-18 minutes, naturally release. While the meat is cooking soak your rice.
When the pressure releases strain the stock to remove the whole spices. Warm a lug of oil in a pot.

Stir in the whole spices - cumin seeds, cloves, black pepper, cinnamon sticks and Cook until they crackle and you can smell the aroma. Put the chopped onions into the pot and saute until they caramelize (8 minutes or so).

Stir in the garlic and ginger paste, saute for another minute. Stir in the chopped or ground green chillies if using. Stir in the coriander powder, red chilli powder, and 1 tsp of salt. Cook for another 30 (Stir in a splash of water if it starts to burn).
In go the beef chunks, stir for a minute so they can absorb the spices and flavors. Stir in the rice and the strained stock.

Put in 2.5 tsp of salt, bring to a boil and cook partially covered until the water is more or less dry and the pulao is done. If the rice is still not cooked shut the lid and turn the heat down, keeping it on low till cooked.

alternate_methods.label: Alternate documented method
instructions: In a large pot, (I use a 6 qt stockpot), Stir in goat meat, black and green cardamom pods, cloves, black cumin, coriander seeds, cinnamon stick, bay leaf, black pepper berries, salt, whole onion marked with an 'X', ginger, garlic and water. Put stockpot on low-medium heat and let it simmer till the meat is tender. Keep checking the meat every 20.
To tenderise, the meat will take approximately 1-1 1/2 hour. The meat I use takes 1 hour and 20 minutes to tenderise. The garlic cloves will soften up as they cook.

When the meat is tender, in a fine sieve, drain the stock. The rest of the spices will stick to the meat, do not worry about that and please don't wash it off, or you'll lose the flavour of the meat. In a heavy-bottomed pan, Stir in oil, and sliced onions. On medium heat, Cook the onions till caramelised, this will take.
Turn the heat to low. Stir in three and a half cups of stock, the soaked rice and the reserved meat.
Cover pot with a teacloth (or kitchen paper towel) and Put lid on top. Allow rice to cook for 20 minutes. Turn the heat off and allow the rice to settle and rest for 15-20 minutes.

variants.name: Zafrani Pulao (Saffron Rice)
instructions: Stir in the saffron strands to 3 tbsp of warm doodh (milk). Stir gently and let sit for at least 20 minutes.
Warm 2 tbsp ghee in a small karai (wok) on medium heat. Stir in the kaaju (cashews) first — they take longest. Stir for 60-90 seconds until pale golden.

In a heavy degh (pot), heat the remaining 2 tbsp fresh ghee plus the fruit-flavoured ghee from step 2 on medium heat. Stir in the whole spices — elaichi (cardamom), dalchini (cinnamon), laung (cloves).
Stir in 3 cups of water to the pot. Stir in cheeni (sugar) and namak (salt). Bring to a boil.
Cover the degh with foil pressed tight around the edges, and then the lid. Cook on lowest heat for 15-18 minutes.

variants.name: Creamy Rabri — Lahori Style
instructions: Pour milk into a wide, heavy-bottomed karahi (wider = more surface area = faster reduction and more cream skins). Stir in cardamom pods. Bring to a boil over medium-high heat, stirring to prevent scorching.
As the milk simmers, a cream skin (malai) will form on the surface every 8-10 minutes. Do NOT stir it back into the milk.
Continue on medium-low heat for 60-75 minutes, collecting skins every 8-10 minutes and letting the milk reduce. Stir the bottom gently each time you collect a skin.
After 60-75 minutes, the milk will have reduced to about 1/3 of its original volume and will be thick, creamy, and pale golden. Stir gently to incorporate.
Stir in sugar and stir to dissolve. Stir in saffron milk. Cook for another 5 minutes, and then remove from heat.

Pour into a wide, flat serving dish (thaal) or individual clay pots. Let cool to room temperature, and then refrigerate for at least 2 hours. Garnish with slivered almonds, pistachios, and a few saffron strands before serving.

variants.name: Traditional Rabri
instructions: Stir in the zafran (saffron) threads and stir once. Let it sit for at least 15 minutes — the milk will turn a deep golden orange and smell extraordinary.

REDUCE THE MILK — PHASE 1: Pour all 2 litres of doodh (full-fat milk) into a wide, heavy-bottomed degh (pot) or pateela (saucepan). Bring to a rolling boil over high heat, stirring constantly to prevent a skin from sticking to the bottom. Once boiling, reduce to medium heat.
DO NOT stir it back in yet.

Once the milk has reduced to roughly half its original volume (about 45-60 minutes in), Stir in the cheeni (sugar) and the bloomed saffron along with its soaking liquid. Stir well to dissolve the sugar.
Continue simmering and folding malai layers for another 30-40 minutes.
Take the pot off heat. Stir in elaichi powder (cardamom) and kewra water (if using).
Transfer the rabri into a wide serving bartan (bowl) or individual cups. Let it cool to room temperature, and then refrigerate for at least 2 hours — ideally overnight.

Here is the most important moment. Remove the pan from heat for 30 seconds to let it cool slightly. Whisk your room-temperature dahi (yoghurt) vigorously in its bowl until completely smooth.
Stir in the browned lamb back into the masala and stir to coat every piece. Stir in 1 cup of warm water. Season with salt.
After 50 minutes, lift the lid.
Turn off the heat and let the Rogan Josh sit uncovered for 5 minutes before serving.

instructions: Soak dried Kashmiri chilies in warm water for 20 minutes. Blend to a smooth, vibrant red paste. This is your color and mild heat base.
Warm ghee in a heavy-bottomed pot until smoking. Stir in black cardamom, cloves, and cinnamon.

Stir in fresh ginger and garlic. Stir-Cook 2 minutes. Stir in the Kashmiri chili paste and cook, stirring, for 5 minutes until the oil separates from the paste — you'll see the ghee coming out at the edges.
Stir in fennel powder, dried ginger powder, and salt. Stir well and cook 2 more minutes.
Stir in the meat and stir vigorously to coat every piece. Cook on high heat 8-10 minutes, stirring constantly, until the meat is seared and coated in the red masala.
Stir in 2 cups water. Bring to a boil, and then cover and simmer on low heat 60-90 minutes until the mutton is tender.
Remove lid and cook on medium-high heat for 5-10 minutes, stirring, until excess water evaporates and the gravy clings to the meat.

In a large bowl or paraat (wide kneading bowl), Mix the maida (refined white flour), namak (salt). Stir in 1 egg, tel (oil), dahi (yoghurt), and the foamy yeast mixture. Stir in the remaining lukewarm water, a little at a time, until the dough comes together in a.
Turn the dough out onto a lightly oiled surface (use a few drops of oil, not flour). Knead for 8-10 minutes using the heel of your hand — push, fold, turn, repeat.

Turn your oven to its absolute maximum heat — 250°C (480°F) or as high as it goes. Let the oven preheat for at least 30 minutes with the pan inside.

Punch the risen dough down gently with your fist to release the gas. On a lightly floured surface, roll each portion into an oval shape about 25cm long and 12cm wide and about 5mm thick — think a rounded teardrop or tongue shape.

Very carefully slide 1-2 naans at a time (however many fit without touching) onto your preheated cast-iron pan or baking stone. Bake for 4-6 minutes. Watch carefully — at this high heat things happen fast.
Naan is at its absolute best in the first 10 minutes.

ingredients.text: 1 cup maida (refined white flour / all-purpose flour)
1 cup gehun ka atta (whole wheat flour)

instructions: In a large bowl, Mix maida, atta, and salt. Stir in the oil and rub it into the flour with your fingertips until the flour looks like damp sand — this coats the flour proteins and makes the dough extensible rather than elastic. and then Stir in warm.
REST THE DOUGH — PROPERLY: This is non-negotiable. Divide the dough into 4 balls, brush with a tiny bit of oil, cover with a damp cloth, and rest for AT LEAST 30 minutes. 45–60 minutes is better.

Put a heavy karahi (wok) or large tawa upside down on the stove over medium-high heat. Let it heat for 3–4 minutes until very hot. The roti will be draped over the convex underside of the karahi to cook.
On a very lightly floured chakla (rolling board), take one rested dough ball and begin rolling with your belan (rolling pin). Roll, rotate, roll, rotate — working from the centre outward.
This is the nerve-wracking part. Loosely roll the thin roti around your belan (like a scroll), and then carry it over to the inverted karahi and unroll it over the convex surface.
The roti cooks fast — 30 to 45 seconds per side on a properly preheated surface. Cook another 20–30 seconds on this side.

ingredients.text: 1.5 tbsp adrak lahsun paste (ginger garlic paste)
8 whole sabut kali mirch (whole black peppercorns)

instructions: Warm ghee in a heavy-bottomed pot until very hot. Stir in whole spices (badi elaichi, laung, kali mirch) and sizzle 30 seconds. Stir in gosht and cook on very high heat until deeply browned on all sides — about 10 minutes.
Stir in roughly sliced piyaz and cook until golden. Stir in adrak lahsun paste and cook 2 minutes. Stir in tamatar, laal mirch powder, haldi, and salt.

This is the Balochi technique — cover tightly and cook on low heat for 30-35 minutes, allowing meat to cook in its own steam and juices. Check every 10 minutes. Stir in just a splash of water only if it's sticking.
Once meat is nearly tender, Stir in paalak leaves. Mix into the concentrated masala and meat. Cover and cook 10-12 minutes on low heat.
Remove lid and cook on medium-high heat for 5 minutes to concentrate the flavours and evaporate excess moisture.
Let rest 5 minutes before serving.

Stir in adrak lahsun paste and cook 2 minutes. Stir in tamatar, laal mirch powder, haldi, and salt. Cook until oil surfaces and masala is thick, about 7-8 minutes.
Stir in chopped bathua to the masala. Mix well and cook uncovered on medium heat for 8-10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until everything melds together and excess moisture evaporates.

instructions: Soak 50g raw cashews in warm water for 20 minutes — this softens them for easier blending. Drain and blend with 4 tablespoons fresh water until completely smooth. Separately, blend 2 medium onions with 2 tablespoons water until completely smooth.

Warm oil in a heavy karahi on medium-high heat. Stir in the raw blended onion paste. Cook the onion paste, stirring frequently, for 8-10 minutes until the raw smell disappears and it turns a pale golden colour.

variants.name: Balochi Sajji — Whole Roasted Chicken
instructions: Using sharp kitchen scissors or a heavy knife, cut along both sides of the backbone and remove it.

In a small bartan (bowl), mix the salt, coarsely ground zeera (cumin), lal mirch (red chilli), kali mirch (black pepper), juice of one nimbu (lemon), and kachri powder into a dry rub — it should be just barely moist from the lemon.

Aim for indirect heat — charcoal on one or two sides of the grill, with the centre clear. The target temperature is around 200-220°C, which is medium-high for a home charcoal grill. Stir in a few pieces of wood (fruit wood like apple or cherry is excellent.

Thread a long, thick skewer through the chicken lengthwise from tail to neck, or Put the butterflied bird skin-side up on the indirect heat side of the grill. Close the grill lid. Cook for 30 minutes without opening.

After 30 minutes, open the lid and baste the chicken generously with melted ghee using a brush or a folded piece of cloth on a stick (the traditional method). Close the lid and cook for another 20-25 minutes. The skin should be turning deep golden-brown and the fat.
For absolute certainty, a meat thermometer should read 74°C (165°F) at the thickest point. The skin should be crackly and deep mahogany-brown.
Move the cooked sajji to a large flat platter and rest for 8-10 minutes under a loose foil tent.

instructions: In a large bartan (bowl), Mix maida (flour), salt, ajwain (carom seeds), and oil. Rub the oil into the flour with your fingertips until it resembles coarse breadcrumbs and holds its shape when you squeeze a handful — this is the 'moyan' technique.

Warm 2 tbsp oil in a karahi (pan) over medium heat. Stir in zeera (cumin seeds) — they should pop and sizzle immediately. Stir in the finely diced pyaz (onion) and Cook for 4–5 minutes until lightly golden.

Divide the rested dough into balls — about 10 equal portions. On a lightly floured surface, roll each ball into a thin oval — about 15 cm long and 8 cm wide, similar in thickness to a thin roti (1–2mm). Cut each oval in half across the middle.

Fold it into a cone shape by overlapping the two corners of the straight edge — one corner folds over the other by about 1 cm. Seal the overlapping edges with a dab of water or a flour-water paste (mix 1 tbsp flour + 2 tbsp water).
Warm oil in a deep karahi (wok) or degh to 160–170°C — lower than you'd think.

Samosas are best served within 10 minutes of frying — they lose their shattering crispness as they cool. Arrange on a plate and serve immediately with hari chutney (green coriander-mint chutney) and imli ki chutney (tamarind chutney).

variants.name: Schezwan Chicken
instructions: Soak dried red chillies in boiling water for 20 minutes until completely softened. Drain and blend into a smooth paste with 2 tablespoons of water. In a small bowl, Mix the blended chilli paste with soy sauce, white vinegar, ketchup, and sugar.
Pat the chicken pieces completely dry. Season with a pinch of salt and a pinch of black pepper. Heat 2 tablespoons of oil in a karahi (wok) over maximum heat until smoking.

Stir in the chunky onion and capsicum pieces. Stir-Cook for 2 minutes over high heat. If you prefer softer vegetables, Stir in 30 seconds more cooking time.
Pour the Schezwan sauce base into the karahi. Stir to coat the vegetables. Let the sauce cook for 1 minute — this 'cooks out' the raw chilli paste flavour and develops the sauce's depth.
Return the seared chicken to the karahi. Pour in 4 tablespoons of water or chicken stock. Toss to coat everything in the sauce.

The sauce should coat each piece of chicken and cling to the vegetables in a thick gloss — not watery, not gluey, but somewhere perfectly in between. Taste one final time: if it tastes sharp and flat, Stir in a pinch more sugar. If it tastes dull, Stir.

instructions: In a large bartan (bowl), Mix the beef keema, lamb keema, squeezed onion, adrak lehsan paste, chopped hara dhania (coriander), podina (mint), lal mirch (red chilli), garam masala, toasted cumin, and namak (salt). knead — yes, actually knead — the mixture with your hands for 3-4 full minutes.
Cover the bartan with cling film and refrigerate for at least 1 hour, ideally 2-3 hours or overnight.
Use wet hands to smooth the surface as you shape it into a sausage roughly 15cm long and 3cm thick.

Light your charcoal grill and wait until the coals are white-grey with no orange flame — this takes 15-20 minutes and is important. Lay the skewers across the grill. You'll hear a satisfying sizzle (sss-sss) immediately — if you don't, the grill isn't hot enough.
